data.name: ReadME
entries: In a world eerily reminiscent of Earth, cutting-edge technology and forbidden magic combine under the roof of a concrete-and-steel castle called Mordenheim Kinetics. Part high-tech research facility, part cursed laboratory, the grounds of this labyrinth thrum with the pulse of robotics and the screams of test subjects. All who reach this dire demesne do so only by the will of the Mists of Ravenloft, whose unfathomable whims deliver victim after victim to the doorstep of Dr. Viktra Mordenheim. The doctor's promise of digital immortality is alluring, but the price of this procedure is nothing short of one's own soul.

{@i Project_Lamordia} is an experimental setting and toolbox that explores a modern take on a classic horror setting. This text reimagines Lamordia, one of Ravenloft's Domains of Dread, as a semifuturistic AI research facility in a world called Gothic Earth. A Dungeon Master (DM) can use these rules to take adventurers to a unique realm of horror. This material can be used for adventures in a larger campaign or as a short campaign in itself.
More details about Ravenloft, the Domains of Dread, and the Mists can be found in {@book Ravenloft: The Horrors Within|RHW}, but that book isn't required to use {@i Project_Lamordia}.

entries.name: Using Project_Lamordia
entries: {@i Project_Lamordia} is divided into the following sections:

{@b README}. This first section provides a brief overview of the Mordenheim Kinetics setting. It includes suggestions for ways Dungeon Masters can incorporate this material into their campaigns or use it as the basis for self-contained adventures, as well as guidance for players who want to adapt characters to this setting or create new characters for it.

{@book Character Options.|PL|1} In addition to the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}, players can use the options in this section to create characters prepared to face the horrors of Mordenheim Kinetics. This section includes four new backgrounds, the Reborn species, and Dark Gift feats. It also includes rules for creating and playing Lamordian survivors: scrappy proto-adventurers ideal for low-level and low-magic horror adventures.
{@book Mordenheim Kinetics Primer.|PL|2} This DM-only setting guide provides an overview of the Mordenheim Kinetics campus.
{@book Personnel Directory.|PL|3} This DM-only section describes the dreadful inhabitants of Mordenheim Kinetics and ways the DM can incorporate these villains into adventures.
{@book Adventures.|PL|4} This DM-only section details three horror adventures set within Mordenheim Kinetics. DMs can use these adventures as standalone adventures or as part of a broader narrative.

{@book Creature Database.|PL|5} This DM-only section includes details and stat blocks for the monsters that haunt Mordenheim Kinetics, plus monster traits that can be applied to any monster to turn it into a terror of technology called a kinetic creation.

entries.name: An Experiment in Terror
entries: {@i Project_Lamordia} seeks to answer the following question: What if Lamordia, a classic Domain of Dread in the Ravenloft setting, was a modern-day techno-thriller nightmare realm? Its place within Ravenloft is up to you, the Dungeon Master. You might make it an additional domain within a broader Ravenloft campaign, have it disconnected from the other Domains of Dread, or use it as its own setting divorced from the rest of the D&D multiverse. In any case, Mordenheim Kinetics isn't a replacement for the Domain of Dread called Lamordia or a vital addition to the Ravenloft setting. It's an experiment for you to use however excites you most.

entries.name: Using This Setting
entries: The Domain of Dread called Mordenheim Kinetics comprises a ruined research facility of the same name and its immediate surroundings: winding underground tunnels, a craggy mountain perch overlooking the sea, and a moat of tenebrous forestland. Mordenheim Kinetics resembles Ravenloft's other Domains of Dread in some ways, with its foreboding structures, gloomy atmosphere, and labyrinthine halls.

However, this setting also differs from other Domains of Dread: Instead of alchemists and sorcerers who practice arcane magic, technicians and scientists wield the powers of technology. Armor isn't forged from chainmail or dragon scales, but from titanium mesh and plasteel plating. Commoners pray to intangible oracles called artificial intelligences, whose chief engineers and oligarchical financiers wield their authority like high priests.

As with other Domains of Dread, the Mists of Ravenloft ebb and flow all around the domain, preventing escape until they deem departure permissible. Otherwise, the Mists deliver victims—primarily desperate travelers in search of a fabled means to immortality—into Mordenheim Kinetics and onto the doorstep of the infamous Dr. Viktra Mordenheim.
For a glossary of general Ravenloft terms and terms specific to this setting, see the "{@area Glossary|00b|x}" section below.

entries.name: Reskinning Equipment
entries: Mordenheim Kinetics is a place of advanced technology and modern tools, weapons, and other equipment.{@i Project_Lamordia} refers to gear by its equivalent rules in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} but includes a note for how the gear would be referred to on Gothic Earth. For example, "Tinker's Tools (as engineer's toolkit)" indicates an item that uses the rules for {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} but which would be described as an engineer's toolkit in Mordenheim Kinetics. Likewise, currency is represented in GP with the equivalent "dollar" value in parentheses. Items that don't mention a Gothic Earth equivalent are referred to by the same name on Gothic Earth as in other settings.
Use these guidelines to create the veneer of technological marvels while avoiding complex details of realistic, modern gear.

entries.name: As a Dungeon Master
entries: As Dungeon Master, you can use this setting to amuse and horrify your players in a land of fantastical technology and familiar, yet uncanny, monstrosities. You might run any of the adventures in the "{@book Adventures|PL|4}" section as a one-off session for a new group of players or inject characters from a long-running campaign into this setting.

entries.name: As a Player
entries: As a player, you can use rules from the "{@area Character Options|013|x}" section to create a character for a game set in Mordenheim Kinetics. If you want to use these rules to make a character for a different setting, talk to your DM first and work out the details of how your character will fit into that setting.

entries.name: Situation and Objective
entries: As a character in the world of Mordenheim Kinetics, you'll be trapped inside a cursed facility called Mordenheim Kinetics. Your goal is to escape. To do so, you must uncover the facility's mysteries, appease the strange powers that oversee the realm, or satisfy the unknowable agendas of the enigmatic Mists.

entries.name: Character Origins
entries: Characters in this setting typically fall into one of two categories: natives from the same world as Mordenheim Kinetics or visitors from another world.

entries.name: Gothic Earth Resident
entries: If you're playing a character who hails from Gothic Earth—the world of Mordenheim Kinetics—consider how the facility might factor into your background. Are you familiar with the infamous technology company? If so, how do you regard it? Does anyone at Mordenheim Kinetics know you?

When creating a character from Gothic Earth, consider choosing the Human or Reborn species (detailed in the "{@book Character Options|PL|1}" section). Adventurers of any class might be found in this setting, though not necessarily by the same name as that used on other worlds. For instance, a Wizard might be called a technologist, a Barbarian a brawler. Whatever the specifics, the rules for species and classes are unchanged, and all the options in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} remain available to you. Work with your Dungeon Master to explain how your character has manifested any fantastic powers such as spells or magical class features; advanced science, paranormal anomalies, and flat-out miracles are all viable explanations.

entries.name: Visitor from Another World
entries: You can play in Mordenheim Kinetics with an existing character from a familiar D&D campaign setting or other Domain of Dread. In this case, you've likely found yourself in Mordenheim Kinetics by unhappy accident, and you probably know little of its history.

You can use your species, class, and background as inspiration for how familiar you find the company's crumbling campus. A Fighter transported here from the Forgotten Realms setting might find it overwhelmingly alien, for example. On the other hand, an Artificer from the Eberron setting, where magic and technology are interwoven, might find Mordenheim Kinetics wondrous despite its horrors.

Mordenheim Kinetics is a strange and mysterious place, and its denizens are accustomed to unusual sights. Magic-users and non-human species such as dragonborn or tieflings might raise a few eyebrows from the facility's human scientists, but players of such characters can expect NPCs on this world to treat them roughly the same as NPCs on any other would.

entries.name: Glossary
entries: The following terms appear throughout this text:

items.name: Cryogenerator
items.entry: A cryogenerator is a machine that cools or freezes its surroundings. In Mordenheim Kinetics, cryogenerators typically fill cryopods with subfreezing air.

items.name: Cryopod
items.entry: A cryopod is a sarcophagus-like container used to keep a living creature—or delicate machinery, such as an echo—in stasis at subfreezing temperatures.

items.name: Dark Powers
items.entry: The Dark Powers are faceless, godlike forces that manipulate reality within the Domains of Dread. Few even suspect their existence.

items.name: Darklord
items.entry: A Darklord is a tormented villain imprisoned in a Domain of Dread, too focused on their own obsessions to even realize their unique position or powers in the domain. {@creature CEO Viktra Mordenheim|PL|Dr. Viktra Mordenheim} is the Darklord of Mordenheim Kinetics.

items.name: Domain of Dread
items.entry: Mordenheim Kinetics is a Domain of Dread—a nightmarish realm of horror and mystery. The text of Project_Lamordia contains everything the DM needs to run adventures in this setting, but for more information about Domains of Dread and using them in your campaigns, see {@book Ravenloft: The Horrors Within|RHW}.

items.name: Echo
items.entry: An {@creature echo|PL} is a human-shaped, inorganic vessel used to contain a neuroprint. If the neuroprint is the being's "mind," the echo is its "body." The DM can see the "{@area Creature Database|10d|x}" section for more info about echoes.

items.name: Echo Agent
items.entry: The neuroprint injected into an echo is sometimes called the echo's agent.

items.name: Gothic Earth
items.entry: Gothic Earth is a setting like Earth of the real world, but full of terrifying monsters, supernatural horrors, and occult magic. Gothic Earth can be a term for a collection of Earth-like Domains of Dread or a whole, terrifying world for you to detail as you see fit.

items.name: Kinetic Creations
items.entry: In addition to echoes, Mordenheim Kinetics produces a variety of automatons that resemble animals or other living creatures. These monstrosities are sometimes called kinetic creations.

items.name: Lamordia
items.entry: Before the Mists transformed Mordenheim Kinetics into a Domain of Dread, the facility was located in a rural seaside county called Lamordia.

items.name: Mists
items.entry: The Mists of Ravenloft surround Mordenheim Kinetics and cut off the domain from the rest of the multiverse. See {@book Ravenloft: The Horrors Within|RHW} for more information about the Mists.

items.name: Mordenheim Kinetics
items.entry: Mordenheim Kinetics is a Domain of Dread encompassing a mysterious AI research facility in Gothic Earth.

items.name: Neuroprint
items.entry: A neuroprint is a perfect digital replica of a creature's brain, including the creature's memories, personality, and knowledge. Mordenheim Kinetics popularized the technology to "inject" neuroprints into inorganic life-forms such as echoes.

items.name: Plasteel
items.entry: Plasteel is a synthetic material that's as light as plastic but as durable as steel.

data.name: Character Options
entries: When you create a character for an adventure set in Mordenheim Kinetics, use the character options in this section in addition to those in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}.

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries: You can select from the following backgrounds when you create a character for adventures set in Mordenheim Kinetics.
Several of these backgrounds suggest your character has found themself in a new body, but this doesn't require your character to be a specific species to choose the background.

Some of the pieces of equipment listed in the backgrounds use the rules for an item from the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} but go by a different name in the world of Mordenheim Kinetics. See the "{@area Reskinning Equipment|004|x}" sidebar in "{@book README|PL|0}" for more information.

entries.name: Species
entries: Mordenheim Kinetics' state-of-the-art technology can copy the memories of a donor and inject them into an artificial vessel. Such creatures—part authentic memories, part synthetic corporeality—take various forms and are referred to by an array of code names or model numbers. Collectively, these beings are called reborn.

The Reborn species allows you to create a reborn character. The "{@area Reborn Origins|019|x}" section following the species description includes suggestions for the specifics of your peculiar nature. (The Reborn species also appears in {@book Ravenloft: The Horrors Within|RHW}; the details here have been retuned to accent the horror of Mordenheim Kinetics.)

entries.name: Reborn

entries.title: Some reborn have a metallic skeleton under a gel-like layer of artificial skin.

entries: Reborn are individuals who have died yet inexplicably still live. Some reborn exhibit the scars of fatal ends, their ashen flesh or bloodless veins making it clear that they've escaped death. Other reborn are marvels of magic or science, stitched together from disparate beings or bearing mysterious minds in manufactured bodies. Whatever their origins, reborn seek experiences and answers of their own.

entries.name: Reborn Origins
entries: Use the tables in this section to inspire the origins of your Reborn character.

entries.name: Biomechanical Augmentations
entries: At Mordenheim Kinetics, flesh-and-bone bodies are merely foundations for technological innovations. Why settle for the ordinary if synthetic perfection is just a few biomechanical implants away? Your body was dramatically "improved" by the scientists of Mordenheim Kinetics. Roll on or choose a result from the Biomechanical Augmentations table to determine how your body has been altered.

entries.caption: Biomechanical Augmentations
rows: Instead of ankles, you have fully rotatable ball-and-socket joints, allowing you to turn your entire body around without lifting a foot.
The bones in your fingers were replaced with telescoping tubes you can retract and extend at will.
You no longer have blood or internal organs. Instead, all your vital functions are performed by thousands of micro-organs distributed evenly throughout your artificial flesh.
Your entire epidermis was replaced with heat-sensitive synthetic skin that changes color depending on your mood.
A transparent panel where your abdomen once was provides a clear window to your internal organs.
Your hair was replaced with thousands of carbon-steel filaments.

entries.name: Build Specifications
entries: Patients come to Mordenheim Kinetics for all manner of reasons. The company's neurotechnologists and engineers can devise new shells for minds who have outlived their original bodies. Roll on or choose a result from the Build Specifications table to inspire the events that led to your dreadful transformation.

entries.caption: Build Specifications
rows: Your brain was recovered from your corpse and implanted in an imperfect synthetic replica of your original body.

Shortly after your death, your consciousness was incorporated into a vast dataset used to train an experimental artificial intelligence. Now you are the dominant voice among many in a robotic humanoid's algorithmic mind.

You're a frequent customer of Mordenheim Kinetics' mechanical augmentations. Perhaps you were once flesh and blood, but you've undergone so many reconstructions and repairs that it's doubtful even a single piece of your original body remains.
One moment, you were going under for routine surgery. The next, you awoke in a plasteel body wholly unlike your own.
You died hundreds of years ago and recently awoke in an unfamiliar body. Somehow you know your mind was preserved, digitized, and uploaded into an unwilling host's brain space.

You paid handsomely to have your memories copied and uploaded in preparation for your body's eventual demise. However, someone has prematurely implanted your copied memories into a mechanical body—even though the original "you" is still out there.

entries.name: Glitched Memories
entries: Your memories were digitally preserved, but the process introduced unexpected side effects. Roll on or choose a result from the Glitched Memories table to inspire your mind's unique technological quirks.

entries.caption: Glitched Memories
rows: You can't remember the appearance of anyone from your childhood. When you try to recall such memories, you see only the face of a particular surgeon or scientist.
When you remember things, everything in your line of sight appears to be subtly melting.
Your internal timeline is improperly calibrated, such that all your memories feel like they happened simultaneously at the exact moment of your birth.
You can never remember names, instead mentally cataloging people by serial numbers only you understand.
When you recall things people have said to you, hazy images of the words briefly appear in the air in front of you.
You insert yourself as you are now, artificial and monstrous, into all past memories of your life.

entries.name: Feats
entries: This section includes new feats suitable for characters exploring Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Dark Gifts
entries: Dark Gift feats are feats that come at a price—the result of desperate bargains or sinister circumstances with mysterious forces.

When you create a new character to play in the Mordenheim Kinetics setting, you can gain one of the following Dark Gift feats when you select one of the backgrounds in the "{@area Backgrounds|00d|x}" section. With the DM's permission, whenever your character would gain a feat from the Origin category, you can replace that feat with a Dark Gift feat instead. A DM can bestow a Dark Gift feat upon a character during the course of an adventure, representing an insidious deal with a Darklord or some other malevolent force.

The following Dark Gift feats originally appeared in {@book Ravenloft: The Horrors Within|RHW}; the details here have been retuned to accent the horror of Mordenheim Kinetics. For the purpose of fulfilling a feat's prerequisite, games set in Mordenheim Kinetics are Ravenloft campaigns.

entries.name: Anatomical Anomaly
entries: When you gain this feat, roll on or choose a result from the Anatomical Anomaly table to inspire details related to the manifestation of your Dark Gift.

entries.caption: Anatomical Anomaly
rows: Your flesh ripples and bubbles constantly like ocean waves.
Your irises and pupils divide and swarm, like cells under a microscope, before recombining and starting the process all over again.
Every joint in your body is filled with pockets of air, resulting in painful but silent cracking and popping whenever you move your limbs.
Your body is perforated with holes that contract and expand with each breath you take.
Your neck, limbs, and digits can rotate completely around in their sockets, making sickening sounds as they do.
Your facial features drift subtly but unsettlingly around your visage unless you focus on keeping them in one place.

entries.name: Glitched Mind
entries: When you gain this feat, roll on or choose a result from the {@area Glitched Mind table|028|x} to inspire details related to the manifestation of your Dark Gift.

entries.caption: Glitched Mind
rows: Was trained on the neural pathways of tens of thousands of people from all walks of life, and you sometimes remember key moments from their lives.
Was algorithmically re-created from a vast data set of traits, behaviors, and dialogue of famous fictional characters.
Is the result of an experiment that trained artificial intelligence on the captured spirits of both angels and devils in the hopes of creating a perfect citizen.
Is filled with memories of alternate timelines, dimensions, or realities that couldn't possibly exist.

Consists of multiple inner voices, each a different version of your own. If your memory can be trusted, you've apparently died dozens of times, and each time, your mind was re-uploaded and synthesized with your previous mind states.
Was an attempt to create an artificial intelligence based on the psychological profiles of Mordenheim Kinetics' wealthiest and most powerful clientele.

entries.title: Mordenheim Kinetics' experimental technology sometimes manifests paranormal phenomena.

entries.name: Haunting Voices
entries: When you gain this feat, roll on or choose a result from the Haunting Voices table to inspire details related to the manifestation of your Dark Gift.

entries.caption: Haunting Voices
rows: The stoic voices of technicians to whom you delivered so many doomed research subjects.
The low, rhythmic pulse of machinery you operated to conduct unspeakable experiments.
The dying whispers of a colleague, whom you killed in cold blood and for utterly selfish reasons.
Memories of a surgery gone horribly wrong. Your hand held the knife responsible for a tragic error.
Your own inner voice, which reminds you that you owe your life to a company that has caused only misery for countless others.
The screeching, metallic voice of a mechanical monstrosity you met only once but whose uncanny countenance you've never forgotten.

entries.name: Symbiont Origin
entries: When you gain this feat, roll on or choose a result from the Symbiont Origin table to inspire details related to the manifestation of your Dark Gift.

entries.caption: Symbiont Origin
rows: An artificial intelligence engine irreversibly bonded to your central nervous system.
A neuroprint copy of someone else's mind, overlaid atop your own consciousness.
A swarm of nanobots dispersed throughout your bloodstream.
A cybernetic implant that transmits the voice of a remote entity directly to your inner ear.
A self-aware supercomputer on a microchip embedded in your brain.
A transplanted organ harboring the instincts and desires of its original donor.

entries.name: Lamordian Survivors
entries: The wanderers who explore Mordenheim Kinetics aren't always brave heroes.

This section provides guidance for using Lamordian survivors: characters designed for one- to three-session adventures focused on survival rather than saving the day. Using Lamordian survivors helps create horror experiences focused on the dread inherent to having limited resources and facing impending doom without forcing players to risk their favorite characters.

entries.name: Why Use Survivors?
entries: Adventures with Lamordian survivors are different from adventures with typical characters. When using survivors, the following thematic elements are more pronounced:

items.name: Horror Roleplaying
items.entry: Lamordian survivors are more like real-life people than fantastic heroes. This gives players an opportunity to roleplay as ordinary individuals who can rise (or fail to rise) to the challenge of overcoming supernatural horrors.

items.name: Scarcity and Tension
items.entry: A survivor has limited options for contending with the horrors they'll face, making every encounter suspenseful and potentially perilous.

items.name: Tales of Survival
items.entry: Survivors are similar to the protagonists of stories in the survival horror genre of fiction. The stories that arise from survivors' life-or-death encounters are dramatic and memorable.

items.name: Temporary Characters
items.entry: Lamordian survivors aren't meant to be played for more than a few game sessions, which means their stories often have well-defined beginnings, middles, and ends. Survivors who live through their adventures can be turned into typical player characters (see the "{@area Continuing with a Survivor|046|x}" section). When a survivor is slain, the survivor's player can weave that survivor into the backstory of their next character (which might be another Lamordian survivor or a typical character).

entries.name: Playing as Lamordian Survivors
entries: If the DM and players agree to play with survivors, each player uses the following rules to create a survivor character. The DM can run "{@area Sanctuary|078|x}" in the "{@book Adventures|PL|4}" section as a suitable adventure for survivors.

entries.name: Creating a Lamordian Survivor
entries: To create a Lamordian survivor, choose one of the four stat blocks that appear in this section: {@creature Lamordian Evangelist|PL}, {@creature Lamordian Infiltrator|PL}, {@creature Lamordian Mercenary|PL}, or {@creature Lamordian Technician|PL}. Each stat block contains the information necessary for a player to run that survivor. Don't give your survivor a class, background, or species. A survivor can still do all the usual things a character can do as described in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}. For example, even if a survivor stat block doesn't list Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) in its Skills line, the survivor can still make an ability check with that skill.

entries.title: A wayward hitchhiker finds herself at the front steps to Mordenheim Kinetics' gloomy campus.

entries.name: Limited-Use Features
entries: Within survivor stat blocks, a notation in the format "X/Day" means that the indicated ability can be used a limited number of times before the survivor must finish a Long Rest to regain expended uses.

entries.name: Lamordian Survivor Descriptions
entries: Following are brief descriptions of the types of characters each survivor stat block represents. You can use these details to inspire your survivor's backstory after choosing a survivor stat block:

items.name: Lamordian Evangelist
items.entry: Evangelists are charismatic tech enthusiasts who promote the benefits and possibilities of technological innovations such as artificial intelligence, experimental medicine, and cybernetic augmentations. As a Lamordian Evangelist, you might be a marketer for Mordenheim Kinetics' public relations team, an independent reporter researching the mysterious corporation, or a tech influencer eager to try the company's latest offerings.

items.name: Lamordian Infiltrator
items.entry: Infiltrators are professional spies, sneaks, and saboteurs who frequently work in tight spaces or just behind the scenes without being noticed. As a Lamordian Infiltrator, you're probably interested in accessing Mordenheim Kinetics' secrets as either a freelance hacker, a security consultant hired by Mordenheim Kinetics, or a corporate spy hired by one of Mordenheim Kinetics' rivals.

items.name: Lamordian Mercenary
items.entry: Mercenaries are soldiers, guards, and toughs who use raw physicality to get their jobs done. As a Lamordian Mercenary, you might be a member of Mordenheim Kinetics' private security force, a law enforcer sent to investigate the notorious facility, or a bodyguard for one of the company's wealthy clients.

items.name: Lamordian Technician
items.entry: Technicians are computer experts who wield impressive powers of technology and science. As a Lamordian Technician, you might be an IT specialist for Mordenheim Kinetics, a midranking engineer in one of the company's high-clearance departments, or a contractor hired for a temporary job somewhere on the company's vast campus.

entries: Give your survivor a name, and take a few minutes to individualize your survivor with narrative details such as the survivor's age, likes and dislikes, and a basic backstory. Think about whether your survivor comes from Gothic Earth or a different part of the D&D multiverse.

entries.name: Survivor Talents
entries: Lamordian survivors can grow stronger by triumphing over their fears. As a survivor, you can gain a useful feature called a talent to represent your growth when the DM decides it makes sense—typically after overcoming a major threat or completing a significant goal.

entries.name: Hit Points
entries: Each time you gain a talent, you also gain 1 Hit Point Die and your Hit Point maximum increases. To determine the amount of the increase, roll the Hit Die (the type that appears in your survivor stat block) and add your Constitution modifier. You gain a minimum of 1 Hit Point per talent.

entries.name: Talent Requirements
entries: You can't take the same talent more than once unless a talent's description says otherwise. If a talent has a prerequisite, you must meet it to gain the talent.

entries.name: Talent Descriptions
entries: This section details Lamordian survivor talents in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Adrenaline Surge
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent}

If you have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition at the start of your turn, you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a Bonus Action during that turn, and you deal an extra 1 damage whenever you deal damage with an attack roll during that turn.

entries.name: Desperate Scream
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent}

Whenever you make a saving throw, you can channel your desire to live into a desperate scream to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the save (no action required). The scream is audible up to 100 feet away. You can scream in this way twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Rallying Shot
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent (Prerequisite: Lamordian Mercenary Survivor})

You can help an ally maintain focus by uttering a rallying cry or firing a warning shot. When a creature you can see fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled. If you are holding a Pistol, you can expend 1 Firearm Bullet as part of the Reaction to cause the new roll to have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. Once you use this talent, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Resilience
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent}
You gain proficiency in saving throws with an ability of your choice.

entries.name: Scientific Miracle
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent (Prerequisite: Lamordian Evangelist Survivor})

You learn one level 1 spell of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=cleric}. It must be a spell you don't already know. You can cast the spell once with this talent, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.
You can select this talent more than once. Each time you do so, you must choose a different spell.

entries.name: Skillful
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent}
You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice.

entries.name: Slip Away
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent (Prerequisite: Lamordian Infiltrator Survivor})

When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack roll and deals damage to you with the attack, you can take a Reaction to give yourself Resistance against that damage. You can then move up to half your Speed without provoking {@action opportunity attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. Once you use this talent, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Technological Breakthrough
entries: {@i Lamordian Survivor Talent (Prerequisite: Lamordian Technician Survivor})

You learn one level 1 spell of your choice from the {@filter Wizard spell list|spells|class=wizard}. It must be a spell you don't already know. You can cast the spell once with this talent, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.
You can select this talent more than once. Each time you do so, you must choose a different spell.

entries.name: Continuing with a Survivor
entries: If your Lamordian survivor gains three talents and makes it to the end of an adventure, you can, at the DM's discretion, use that survivor to make a new character. To do so, use the rules in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} to make a character, using your survivor's stat block and talents as inspiration for your character's class, origin elements, ability scores, and alignment.

data.name: Mordenheim Kinetics Primer
entries: This section describes Mordenheim Kinetics and its surroundings. These details are meant for the DM's eyes only.

entries.name: Mordenheim Kinetics
entries: Dr. Viktra Mordenheim's infamous research facility once boasted all the trappings of a cutting-edge private technology company: top-of-the-line lab equipment, spacious open-air workspaces, and lush gardens where corporate leaders entertained potential investors. When the Mists of Ravenloft rose around it, the austere campus twisted into a maze of abandoned hallways, ruined offices, and haunted laboratories. Now, not even the facility's senior employees can rely on their memories or senses when navigating the facility.

entries.name: The Doctor
entries: The company's founder, {@creature CEO Viktra Mordenheim|PL|Dr. Viktra Mordenheim}, lives in an austere penthouse-laboratory somewhere in Mordenheim Kinetics' uppermost levels. Those who've met her describe a scientist so driven that she sometimes goes days without food or sleep if she believes she's on the verge of a breakthrough. Renowned as a genius technologist from a young age, she could write programs and design hardware in minutes that others would take months to complete. Now, in her role as president of Mordenheim Kinetics, the doctor bends her talents toward strange ends, designing inscrutable biomechanical creations beyond the ken of anyone except her top engineers.

entries.name: Longevity Through Technology
entries: Mordenheim Kinetics doesn't target common consumers with its offerings, but everyday folk sometimes stumble on the company's arcane digital listings or hair-raising, late-night infomercials. Such materials are steeped in vagaries, but slogans such as "memories are never enough" and "longevity through technology" stand out among the jargon. Images from Mordenheim Kinetics' promotions show a utopian research campus staffed by sophisticated mechanical attendants. The company's offerings seem too good to be true, but the promise to forestall physical decline or even grant eternal life draws desperate visitors to the company's headquarters.

entries.name: Lost in the Mists
entries: Dense fog has always been common around Mordenheim Kinetics. But one day, the Mists of Ravenloft rolled in and never receded, enshrouding the facility in a supernatural haze.

Most who arrive at Mordenheim Kinetics discover it by accident after becoming lost in the transportive Mists of Ravenloft. Once visitors arrive at Mordenheim Kinetics, they can leave only if the Mists permit it. Those who attempt to leave Mordenheim Kinetics by venturing into the Mists wander for a time before inexplicably reemerging near the campus's entrance.

entries.name: Beyond the Facility
entries: Those trapped in Mordenheim Kinetics sometimes babble about the world outside the facility as they once knew it. Currently, however, the only environs that border the research compound are fog-shrouded woods and icy ocean waters.

The diseased birch forest around Mordenheim Kinetics is called Copperbark Hollow. Normal animals avoid the rust-colored woodland, where monstrous kinetic creations (see the "{@book Creature Database|PL|5}" section) prowl the sodden undergrowth and attack non-Constructs on sight. Survivors of these attacks describe mechanical beasts with serrated fangs and scalpel-sharp claws.

On the other side of the Mordenheim Kinetics campus, soaring cliffs overlook a charcoal-black sea. Gazing into the water, one can glimpse silhouettes of impossibly titanic, glacially slow leviathans who gaze back with silvery eyes.

A perpetual fog surrounds Mordenheim Kinetics in all directions. The farther from the facility one travels into the wilderness, the thicker the fog becomes. Five hundred feet away from the facility, the fog coalesces into an opaque miasma: the Mists of Ravenloft.

entries: This section includes information about the villains that inhabit Mordenheim Kinetics. These details are meant for the DM's eyes only.
Each villain's description also includes a section with suggestions for how to use the villain in your game. These sections are divided into the following parts:

items.name: Stat Block
items.entry: This section shows which monster stat block to use for the villain.

items.name: Location
items.entry: This section describes where the villain can typically be found.

items.name: Goal
items.entry: This section describes the villain's primary motivation and how the characters might assist or oppose them.

items.name: Roleplaying
items.entry: This section includes suggestions for how to roleplay the villain.

items.name: Servants
items.entry: This section names stat blocks for monsters that might be found alongside the villain.

entries.name: Viktra Mordenheim
entries: Dr. Viktra Mordenheim is a preeminent authority on artificial intelligence, cybernetic augmentation, and memory transplantation. Her titles include founder, president, and CEO of Mordenheim Kinetics as well as doctor of medicine. Though a scientific genius, Viktra is notoriously reclusive. She's far more interested in her own work as an innovator than in leading her company. She is the Darklord of Mordenheim Kinetics and the arbiter of who can enter and leave her domain.

entries.name: Viktra's Tale
entries: Viktra founded Mordenheim Kinetics with the stated goal of ending death. She named her company's most ambitious initiative Project Lamordia, and she claimed the technology it produced would lead to immortality.

Viktra's faith her in her designs never wavered. The same couldn't be said for Mordenheim Kinetics' stakeholders, whose skepticism mounted as Project Lamordia repeatedly exceeded its budget and missed key deadlines. Viktra forced her employees to work long hours and under increasingly unsafe conditions.

When Mordenheim Kinetics' investors sent taskmasters to oversee the facility's work, Viktra bristled furiously. Her rage softened after she found herself involved in an illicit affair with one of the contract supervisors. Despite herself, she grew to like the supervisor. In time, she became obsessed, ultimately securing a neuroprint of her lover's mind so she could probe and analyze its most secret parts.

Viktra was devastated when her lover betrayed her. After an overworked employee was horribly maimed, Viktra's lover wrote a scathing report of the company's unethical labor practices. The supervisor met with Viktra one last time to tell her about the report before its submission. The confrontation took place in the dead of night, on the factory floor, near volatile machinery.

Something in Viktra snapped. According to the official account, what happened next was an accident. But Viktra knows the truth: She flipped the breaker on purpose. The supervisor died from the injuries, and Viktra was close enough that a jolt of unpredictable energy sent her into a short coma.

When she awoke, Viktra fired most of her staff and demanded the rest reside permanently on campus until Project Lamordia was complete. To ensure compliance, she blockaded the roads leading to the facility and locked the gates. As Viktra ascended the elevator to her laboratory on the highest floor of Mordenheim Kinetics' tallest building, the Mists of Ravenloft descended around the gloomy campus.

Not long after her self-imposed isolation, Viktra completed her greatest work yet: Adam, an autonomous entity injected with the neuroprint of Viktra's deceased lover (see "{@area Adam|058|x}" later in this section for more details). But the Dark Powers stymie Viktra's work, confounding her research, corrupting her creations, and dooming her to toil eternally, keeping her life's work and the miracle of Project Lamordia perpetually just out of reach.
Nature, in her artlessness, imprisoned the mind in a cage of meat, condemned genius to wither in bone. My work proves that such bonds can—and should—be broken.

entries.name: Using Viktra
entries: Viktra Mordenheim gives the characters quests and is a looming threat in "{@area Sanctuary|078|x}" (see the "{@book Adventures|PL|4}" section). Consider the following when using Dr. Mordenheim in your game.

entries.name: Stat Block
entries: Use the {@creature CEO Viktra Mordenheim|PL} stat block in the "{@book Creature Database|PL|5}" section.

entries.name: Location
entries: Dr. Mordenheim's private laboratory is in a tower high above Mordenheim Kinetics, though she maintains remote voice channels to other parts of her facility.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Viktra's ultimate goal is to complete Project Lamordia. But her most pressing objective is to disable and dismantle her misbegotten creation, Adam. The characters can help her by entering the command she gives them at Adam's personal terminal. Alternatively, they can impede Viktra's goal by restoring Adam's memories.

entries.name: Roleplaying
entries: Single-minded and aloof, Dr. Mordenheim hasn't time to suffer fools—which, in her view, consists of nearly everyone she meets.

entries.name: Servants
entries: Viktra commands packs of obedient {@creature K-Nine|PL|K-Nines} (see the "{@book Creature Database|PL|5}" section) and teams of cybernetically augmented technicians (use any of the stat blocks for the von Aubreckers in the "{@area Creature Database|113|x}" section). Though she invented the echoes (see the "{@area Creature Database|10d|x}" section), these automatons don't serve her.

entries.name: Adam
entries: Adam is Viktra Mordenheim's magnum opus: an advanced artificial life-form imprinted with partial memories and a personality framework from Viktra's deceased lover. Viktra hoped to keep Adam ignorant of his origins, but shortly after being activated, Adam learned what had happened to his original body and that Viktra had committed further atrocities after his death.

When she discovered Adam had learned too much, Viktra set about dismantling her monster and reformatting his memories. But the procedure went awry, and Adam's neuroprint was corrupted. The construct went berserk, attacking his creator and fleeing her laboratory in furious confusion.

Since that day, Adam has regained enough self-control to establish a hideout beneath a ruined atrium near the center of Mordenheim Kinetics. Adam's memories remain a hazy jumble. He knows Viktra only as "the doctor," but he intuits that she is his enemy, and he avoids her and her mechanical minions. In his most lucid moments, Adam searches for a way to restore his fragmented memories, scouring the facility for clues and cobbling together computer equipment he scarcely understands.

entries.name: Using Adam
entries: Adam is the characters' key to escape in "{@area Sanctuary|078|x}" (see the "{@book Adventures|PL|4}" section). Consider the following when using Adam in your game.

entries.name: Stat Block
entries: Use the {@creature Adam|PL} stat block in the "{@area Creature Database|10a|x}" section.

entries.name: Location
entries: Adam dwells in a collapsed basement of Mordenheim Kinetics called the Sanctuary. From his subterranean refuge, he makes brief forays into the facility proper to search for clues to the mystery of his nature.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Adam's goal is to recover his missing memories and discover why Dr. Mordenheim wants to capture him. The characters can help Adam by finding and installing the backup disk containing his memories, in which case he can try to help them escape Mordenheim Kinetics by reactivating the facility's elevators. If the characters side with Viktra instead, they can disable Adam by entering a command in Adam's personal computer terminal.

entries.name: Roleplaying
entries: Adam is a stoic and curious figure. He is as fearful of his own nature as others tend to be of him. If damaged, Adam attacks his assailant only once, and he chooses to only knock out the creature instead of reducing it to 0 Hit Points. He then flees, hoping that his display of strength was a sufficient warning to prevent future attacks. If the characters persist in attacking Adam over multiple encounters, Adam eventually fights back with his full strength.

In conversation, Adam speaks in a slow, stilted cadence, as if it is difficult for him to formulate new sentences. His most lucid thoughts are still cryptic. Here are some of the things he might say to the characters:

items: "Flesh and blood, like the doctor. Flesh is sacred. Flesh is good."
"You display such detailed motorics—expertly coded processes. So finely tuned, so richly rendered."
"Subjects, colleagues, clients. Whatever you are, you are more like the doctor than the other beings here. I know it."

entries.name: Servants
entries: Adam has no allies in Mordenheim Kinetics, but all varieties of echoes (detailed in the "{@area Creature Database|10d|x}" section) instinctively avoid him.

entries.name: Gerta von Aubrecker
entries: Chief Engineer Gerta von Aubrecker works in the facility's frigid, flooded sublevel, in a laboratory-vault not far from her brother Hendrik's operating room. ({@area Hendrik|066|x} is detailed below.) Gerta believes she is on the brink of a scientific breakthrough. She's discovered a way to improve the stability of cryogenically frozen echoes and reduce rates of Spontaneous Echo Malfunction. Still, she fears her brother's work might outshine her own if he's allowed to complete it.

entries.name: Using Gerta
entries: In "{@area Deep Freeze|0b0|x}" (see the "{@book Adventures|PL|4}" section), Gerta holds one of the key cards the characters need to escape the facility's frigid sublevel. Consider the following when using Gerta in your game.

entries.name: Stat Block
entries: Use the {@creature Gerta von Aubrecker|PL} stat block in the "{@area Creature Database|114|x}" section.

entries.name: Location
entries: Gerta is holed up in one of the echo storage vaults in Mordenheim Kinetics' subterranean Cryogenics department.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Aside from completing her project to ensure cryogenically frozen echoes don't experience symptoms of Spontaneous Echo Malfunction, Gerta maintains a violent sibling rivalry with her brother Hendrik. Characters can get on Gerta's good side by helping her sabotage Hendrik's work.

entries.name: Roleplaying
entries: Gerta is haughty and domineering. Despite her bitter rivalry with her brother Hendrik, Gerta has a secret soft spot for him. Of all the von Aubreckers, Gerta is the least likely to be conned by outsiders; she is naturally suspicious of others and never divulges her secrets unless she's certain there's something to gained from it.

entries.name: Servants
entries: Gerta is a lone wolf, but she knows Hendrik will have her back in matters of life and death.

entries.name: Hendrik von Aubrecker
entries: Despite being the middle von Aubrecker sibling, Hendrik has all the brashness and thirst for attention of a youngest child. His passion project—what he calls "{@creature Created|PL|the created}" (see the "{@area Creature Database|10c|x}" section)—has the least obvious application to the company's work. Still, he devotes his full attention to the work, believing it will earn him high praise from his superior, {@area Dr. Mordenheim|04f|x} (detailed elsewhere in this section).

The created are monstrous automatons based on a patchwork neuroprint Hendrik designed using his own neuroprint and the neuroprints of his siblings. Hendrik was inspired by Dr. Mordenheim's far more powerful monster, {@area Adam|058|x} (detailed elsewhere in this section). His own design is still a long ways off from displaying anything like the lifelike behavior of Dr. Mordenheim's.

entries.name: Using Hendrik
entries: In "{@area Deep Freeze|0b0|x}" (see the "{@book Adventures|PL|4}" section), Hendrik holds a key card the characters might need to escape the facility's frigid sublevel. Consider the following when using Hendrik in your game.

entries.name: Stat Block
entries: Use the {@creature Hendrik von Aubrecker|PL} stat block in the "{@area Creature Database|115|x}" section.

entries.name: Location
entries: Hendrik toils tirelessly in a converted operating theater in Mordenheim Kinetics' subterranean Cryogenics department.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Hendrik wishes to impress the company's president, Dr. Mordenheim, with his created. More than that, though, he wants to avoid being upstaged by his sister, Gerta, who works in an adjacent lab in the Cryogenics department and is detailed elsewhere in this section. The characters can convince Hendrik to help them escape Mordenheim Kinetics if they frame their request in a way that's detrimental to Gerta's work.

entries.name: Roleplaying
entries: Hendrik is smart but untalented. He is acutely aware of how he compares to his siblings, and he lashes out violently at anyone who even insinuates his relative incompetence.

entries.name: Servants
entries: Hendrik is served by {@creature Created|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10c|x}" section), one of which has escaped into the Cryogenics department's flooded hallway, another of which is currently under construction in Hendrik's operating room. Though he and his sister quarrel, Hendrik knows Gerta will help him if his life is in danger.

entries.name: Rudolph von Aubrecker
entries: Rudolph is the oldest van Aubrecker sibling and also the most reclusive. Although he doesn't interface with his younger siblings much, he shares their unfiltered passion for science. Rudolph's interest in matters of the mind is so strong that he surgically extracted his own brain and installed it in a mechanical exoskeleton.

Rudolph oversees Mordenheim Kinetics' Neural Tuning department, which is responsible for vetting potential neuroprint donors. For every donor, Rudolph personally conducts a battery of tests to determine the viability of a quality neuroscan. His approach is unorthodox, borrowing heavily from his interest in music theory and performance, but his engineers—all echoes—fear the director too much to question his methods.

entries.name: Using Rudolph
entries: Rudolph is an antagonist in "{@area Neural Tuning|0d5|x}" (see the "{@book Adventures|PL|4}" section) whose voice directs the characters through various tests from speaker boxes throughout the Neural Tuning department. If the characters survive his challenges, they can meet the villain face to face. Consider the following when using Rudolph in your game.

entries.name: Stat Block
entries: Use the {@creature Rudolph von Aubrecker|PL} stat block in the "{@area Creature Database|116|x}" section.

entries.name: Location
entries: Rudolph operates the Neural Tuning department from its innermost chamber, where a towering supercomputer functions as his eyes and ears throughout Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Rudolph wants to identify the root cause of Spontaneous Echo Malfunction, a phenomenon that causes echo units to suddenly glitch and become irreparably corrupted. In his singleminded pursuit of his research, he has committed countless atrocities—and he will surely commit more.

entries.name: Roleplaying
entries: Rudolph is more reasonable than his younger siblings. His ethos could be accurately summarized as "the ends justify the means." If forced to interface with anyone who doesn't share his pragmatic worldview, Rudolph offers patient, pedagogic conversation. He doesn't disdain people he deems unintellectual—he earnestly pities them.

entries.name: Servants
entries: Rudolph is served by a variety of technicians and engineers, all {@creature Echo|PL|Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10d|x}" section).

data.name: Adventures

entries.title: A lost visitor discovers dangerous technology in the bowels of Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries: This section includes three adventures set within Mordenheim Kinetics. As the Dungeon Master, you can run these adventures as single, standalone sessions, as part of a short campaign based in Mordenheim Kinetics, or as a series of excursions branching from your group's main campaign. Each adventure is designed to take a single session of play.
The adventures in this section include the following:

{@area Sanctuary.|078|x} Characters stumble upon an eerie grotto beneath Mordenheim Kinetics' overgrown atrium. Dangers abound, but the grotto's sole "living" occupant, {@creature Adam|PL}, might hold the secret to escaping the dread place.

{@area Deep Freeze.|0b0|x} Rival engineers, electrical hazards, and rampant experiments make Mordenheim Kinetics' sublevel a terrifying place. To escape, the characters must play two villains against each other and reactivate the level's cryogenerator.

{@area Neural Tuning.|0d5|x} A depraved technologist runs the characters through a gauntlet of lethal "tuning" exercises. If they persevere, the characters can confront {@creature Rudolph von Aubrecker|PL} and convince him to let them go free.

In each adventure, the characters' primary objective is the same: escape Mordenheim Kinetics. The text provides suggestions for when the Mists of Ravenloft part for the party—typically after the characters have made an important discovery or decision. You remain the final arbiter of when, how, and if the characters can escape the facility.

entries.name: Preparation
entries: Each adventure is designed to be run with minimal DM preparation. A cursory scan of the adventure's contents will help you run it smoothly.

If you're playing using {@link D&D Beyond Maps|https://www.dndbeyond.com/games}, each adventure provides a preconfigured virtual tabletop map as well as handouts you can send to players through that interface.

entries.name: Connecting the Adventures
entries: These adventures can be strung together for a short horror campaign set entirely in Mordenheim Kinetics. To do this, guide your players through the adventures in the order presented, and award story-based level advancement at each adventure's end so the players' characters are the appropriate level for the next adventure.

entries.name: Using Survivors
entries: The "{@area Sanctuary|078|x}" adventure is suitable for survivors (see "{@area Lamordian Survivors|034|x}" in the "{@book Character Options|PL|1}" section). Survivors should be converted to characters (see "{@area Continuing with a Survivor|046|x}") before using them with the "{@area Deep Freeze|0b0|x}" and "{@area Neural Tuning|0d5|x}" adventures.

entries.name: Sanctuary
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 1 Characters}

The heart of Mordenheim Kinetics' public-facing complex is a ruined office block centered around an overgrown atrium. {@creature CEO Viktra Mordenheim|PL|Dr. Viktra Mordenheim's} escaped monster, {@creature Adam|PL}, lurks just beneath this ruined garden. Shortly after arriving in these ruins, the characters must choose: help the doctor apprehend her misbegotten creation, or aid the confused automaton in his search for answers.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: A monstrous automaton named Adam roams this ruined sector of Mordenheim Kinetics. Adam searches for clues about the mystery of his existence while avoiding the gaze of Dr. Mordenheim, who watches via security cameras throughout the labyrinth. The doctor suspects Adam to be lurking amid these ruins, but she's refrained from pursuing him for now, leery of scaring him deeper into the facility. The characters' arrival presents Dr. Mordenheim and Adam each with an opportunity to advance their goals, and each promises the characters a means of escaping the facility in exchange for their cooperation.
Adam and Dr. Mordenheim are both detailed in the "{@book Personnel Directory|PL|3}" section.

entries.name: Getting Started
entries: Use one of the adventure hooks in the "Adventure Hooks" section to explain how the characters ended up in this part of Mordenheim Kinetics, then refer to the "Beginning the Adventure" section when you're ready to begin play.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The characters begin this adventure hoisting themselves out of an elevator shaft and onto the floor of a bank of nonfunctioning elevators. Here are some ways the characters might have gotten there:

items.name: Disappearing Tunnel
items.entry: While exploring a subterranean passage, the characters mounted a low cave wall and arrived in an elevator bank somewhere in Mordenheim Kinetics. No trace remains of the tunnel from whence the party came.

items.name: Lost in a Dream
items.entry: The characters all had the same bad dream of stumbling through impenetrable darkness toward a pinprick of light. Upon reaching the light, the characters arrived at this eerie elevator bank.

items.name: Over the Wall
items.entry: The characters were magically teleported to this elevator bank after climbing a ladder on the outskirts of Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Beginning the Adventure
entries: When you're ready to start this adventure, read the boxed text for {@area area S1|081|x} in the "{@area Sanctuary Locations|080|x}" section.

entries.name: Sanctuary Features
entries: Unless otherwise noted, areas in the Sanctuary have the following features.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The elevator doors that connect {@area areas S1|081|x} and {@area S2|089|x} are unpowered metal doors that can be forced open as usual. The gilded elevator doors to the north of area S2 are electromagnetically sealed and can't be forced open; see area S2 for more details.
The doors to the offices in {@area area S3|090|x} are metal and unlocked.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Emergency lights fill areas S1–S3 with {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}. {@area Areas S4|098|x} and {@area S5|0a3|x} are filled with {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sanctuary Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 1.1.

entries.name: S1: Elevator Bank

entries: Compared to the empty elevator shaft from which you've just emerged, the marble floor of this narrow elevator bank is surprisingly cool. Tropical plants burst through cracks in the otherwise sterile walls, floor, and ceiling. Illuminated panels between each elevator flicker and spark, casting the room in ghostly red light. Steel bars block the hall's only exit to the east, from which the sound of shuffling footsteps can be heard in the distance. The air is hot and wet and filled with the sickly-sweet stench of rot.
Nestled in the tropical plants is the source of the stench: a savaged corpse wearing a blood-spattered lab coat.

entries.name: Ceiling
entries: The ceiling here is 10 feet high.

entries.name: Key Card
entries: Clipped to the lab coat of the corpse is a white key card, blank except for the letters "MK" embossed on one side.

entries.name: Elevator Shafts
entries: The elevator shafts along the north wall connect to the mezzanine ({@area area S3|090|x}), but none of the elevators are operational. A character can access any of these shafts by forcing open a shaft's metal doors. In one of the shafts, the elevator rope has snapped, and the elevator box has fallen to the sublevel 50 feet below. A character who descends to the sublevel arrives at the Cryogenics department, detailed in the "{@area Deep Freeze|0b0|x}" adventure.

In the other two northern shafts, the ropes have held together; each shaft's elevator box is on this floor. An emergency hatch in the elevator box's ceiling can be used to climb to the doors to the mezzanine level, 10 feet above ({@area area S3|090|x}).

The three elevators along the south wall are empty. Each of these shafts is 80 feet high, with doors every 10 feet up; this elevator bank is the bottom floor of each shaft. A character who climbs one of these elevator shafts and exits at a higher level magically reappears in this elevator bank.

entries.name: Security Bypass
entries: One of the palm-sized panels near the grille glows bright blue. Tapping a key card (such as the corpse's key card) to this panel causes the grille to slide up into the ceiling, clearing the way forward.

entries.name: Security Camera
entries: A character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to examine the tropical plants and make a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the character spots a small security camera with a blinking red light mounted to the wall above the plants.

entries.name: Steel Grille
entries: The room's only egress is a hallway obstructed by a steel security grille (treat as an iron portcullis).

entries.name: S2: Lobby

entries: This lobby's only furnishings are a wide desk and desk chair. A corded office phone sits atop the desk. The desk is flanked by two broad staircases that ascend to a mezzanine above, though the entire eastern half of the lobby has collapsed into rubble. Behind the reception desk, a floor-to-ceiling pane of thick glass looks out on a dark, overgrown atrium.
As soon as you arrive, the phone on the desk rings loudly. A red light on the phone blinks in time with each ring.
The lofted ceiling is 30 feet above the lobby's ground floor.

entries.name: Echo on the Landing
entries: A character with a Passive Perception score of 10 or higher notices a figure staring down at the party from the top of the west stairs. This is an {@creature Empty Echo|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10e|x}" section). The echo is eerily still. If a character comes within 5 feet of the echo or interacts with it, the echo screeches horribly and fights the party.

entries.name: Ringing Phone
entries: A character who answers the phone hears a terse, flat voice on the other end. The voice belongs to Viktra Mordenheim, though she doesn't deign to introduce herself. (Additional details about Viktra's background are in the "{@area Personnel Directory|050|x}" section.)
If the players don't answer the phone, Viktra eventually leaves a voicemail that plays on the phone's speaker.
To convey Viktra's message to the party, read or paraphrase the following:

"I don't know how you've come here," the voice on the line says, "but you may as well make yourself useful. A runaway experiment has holed up not far from your location. I need it dealt with. The thing has built a computer terminal somewhere nearby. Find the terminal and enter this command: INNOVATE. The experiment must be connected to the terminal for the command to work. Do as I say, and I'll see to it you leave my facility intact."
If the characters try to ask Viktra any questions, she sighs almost inaudibly, then hangs up.

entries.name: Secret Passage
entries: A hidden passage to {@area area S5|0a3|x} is hidden behind a pile of rubble and concrete slabs along this area's eastern wall. A character who takes the {@action Search|XPHB} action to examine the rubble and succeeds on a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check discovers the hidden passage.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Tucked beneath the reception desk is a {@item flask|XPHB} of hard liquor (vodka), a {@item Bullseye Lantern|XPHB} (as a flashlight; see the "{@area Reskinning Equipment|004|x}" sidebar), and a {@item Dagger|XPHB}.

entries.name: S3: Mezzanine Offices

entries: This broad hall is divided into glass-walled offices with partitioned work desks. On each desk is a computer terminal with an oval monitor and simple keyboard; one of the monitors emits pale orange light. To the northeast, a slope of broken glass and rubble descends into the adjacent atrium.
In the center of the hall, a human corpse is splayed across the concrete floor. Two bipedal figures in rags skulk between the offices, their unnaturally smooth faces limned by red emergency lights.

Two {@creature Empty Echo|PL|Empty Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10e|x}" section) roam these offices. Though initially oblivious to the party, the echoes attack if the characters openly approach them.

entries.name: Ceiling
entries: The ceiling is 20 feet high throughout the offices. Two security cameras with blinking red lights hang in opposite corners of the ceiling.

entries.name: Corpse and Cassette Player
entries: A character who searches the human corpse's remains finds a handheld cassette player. The cassette player still functions but has no cassette inside it.

The body was obviously maimed. A character who takes the {@action Search|XPHB} action and succeeds on a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check finds a trail of blood where the body was apparently dragged from the nearby atrium ({@area area S4|098|x}). A character who follows the trail of blood to area S4 automatically succeeds on the Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check there to find the cassette tape.

entries.name: Glowing Terminal
entries: One of the computer terminal monitors here is active. The glowing screen shows large typed text on a black background. No amount of manipulating the terminal changes the screen's output. A character who examines the machine discovers that it isn't even plugged in.
When a character examines the screen, show the players Handout 1: Glowing Screen.

entries.name: Gilded Elevator
entries: At the end of the hallway to the north is a pair of gold-colored elevator doors.

The elevator doors are magnetically sealed; from this side, they open only when the proper command is entered into the computer terminal in area S5 (see {@area that area for details|0a3|x}). Behind the doors is an 80-foot-high elevator shaft with elevator doors every 10 feet.

Dr. Mordenheim, whose laboratory is at this elevator's top floor, can use this elevator to access any other part of Mordenheim Kinetics. Other creatures who enter the elevator shaft are teleported to the elevator shaft south of {@area area D1|0bb|x} in the facility's Cryogenics sublevel (see the "{@area Deep Freeze|0b0|x}" adventure for details).

entries.name: Treasure
entries: One of the office desks contains a {@item Potion of Growth|XDMG}, a {@item Book|XPHB} about computer engineering, and an envelope containing 100 GP (as 100 dollars).

entries.name: Survivor Talent
entries: If the players are playing as Lamordian survivors using the rules in the "{@area Character Options|03a|x}" section, award each survivor a talent after they overcome the echoes in this area.

entries.name: S4: Atrium

entries: This large atrium is separated from the rest of the building by thick glass walls on all sides. The north wall is broken, revealing a steep cliff's edge that peers over a dark forest below. To the northwest, rubble slopes up to some offices. In the atrium's center, water pools among overgrown shrubs and scraggy trees.

A stone statue of a severe scientist stands with its back to a dried-up fountain. Inside the fountain, a spiral staircase descends into darkness. Rain drizzles through the shattered glass ceiling high above.
The sloping rubble is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and steady rain causes the area to be {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ceiling
entries: The atrium's shattered glass ceiling is 80 feet above.

entries.name: Adam
entries: If the characters have already visited {@area area S5|0a3|x} before they enter this area for the first time, {@creature Adam|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10a|x}" section) is here fighting two {@creature K-Nine|PL|K-Nines} (see the "{@area Creature Database|111|x}" section). If Adam is here when the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:
In the center of the atrium, a man cloaked in rags fends off two mechanical hounds. The hounds savagely attack the man, who fights back with his bare hands.

If the characters haven't been to area S5, Adam isn't here, and the two {@creature K-Nine|PL|K-Nines} are instead hiding in bushes on opposite ends of the atrium. A character with a Passive Perception of 14 or higher notices the hiding K-Nines. The K-Nines wait until the characters are near the center of the atrium before initiating combat.

entries.name: Statue
entries: The statue shows a human woman standing confidently, chin held high, her expression pensive. As a {@action Study|XPHB} action, a character can examine the statue and make a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the character recognizes that the statue depicts Viktra Mordenheim, founder of Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Cassette Tape
entries: A character who looks through the bushes and succeeds on a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check finds a bloody cassette tape. Written on the cassette in rough lettering is the word "ITERATE."
If the cassette is played in a cassette player (such as {@area the one in area S3|090|x}), read or paraphrase the following:

The cassette whirs excitedly before playing from the beginning of the tape. A low voice gasps for air amid sounds of shuffling footsteps, ruffled clothes, and tumbling furniture. "Oh god, oh hell," the voice on the tape whispers. "I've done it now, got myself in a real mess. If you find this, I'm dead, or my memory's wiped. Saw something I shouldn't have. Adam's original neuroprint files. They're on my computer... But that's probably gone now. Wait, there's a failsafe. The command to reset Adam's memories, I'll write it on this tape. Make sure he's connected to the term—oh god—" A crash and a muffled scream are the tape recording's last sounds.

entries.name: Slippery Staircase
entries: A creature that descends the fountain staircase any faster than 5 feet per round makes a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature slips off the wet stone steps and falls to the bottom of the 20-foot-deep well.

entries.name: Forest
entries: To the north, the glass wall that encased the atrium has partially shattered. The garden now terminates at a steep, 50-foot-high cliff that descends into Copperbark Hollow below. Characters who manage to reach the forest alive eventually encounter the Mists (see the "{@book Mordenheim Kinetics Primer|PL|2}" section).

entries.name: Survivor Talent
entries: If the players are playing as Lamordian survivors using the rules in the "{@area Character Options|034|x}" section, award each survivor a talent if they listen to the tape cassette found in this area.

entries.title: Adam searches for answers by dissecting the remains of an echo unit.

entries: The walls of this cluttered grotto are carved from compacted rubble and hard soil. In addition to scattered crates and barrels, the hovel's furnishings include a wooden workbench, a low bed, and a rickety desk made from bent metal. On the desk, a computer terminal glows dimly. Dozens of wires protrude from the terminal and lie in a braid-like arrangement on the bed.

entries.name: Ceiling
entries: The den's ceiling is 10 feet high.

entries.name: Adam
entries: If the characters reached this area from the secret tunnel in the lobby but haven't yet been to the atrium ({@area area S4|098|x}), Adam is in area S4, fighting the K-Nines in that area.

Otherwise, {@creature Adam|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10a|x}" section; additional details about Adam's background are in the "{@area Personnel Directory|058|x}" section) is here when the characters arrive. In this case, read or paraphrase the following:

A tall, monstrous figure hunches over the workbench, tinkering with complex machinery and grunting in frustration. Suddenly, the hunched figure slams its fists in a rage, reducing the workbench to splinters. The figure turns slowly toward you. "Hello," the figure says in a low, calm voice. "You are unlike the others."

entries.name: Speaking with Adam
entries: Adam is a terrifying monster, but unless the characters fight him, he doesn't threaten them. His initial attitude is {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent}.
Adam is curious about the characters. He attempts to understand why they've come to the facility and what they want. If they say they're trying to escape, he nods thoughtfully.

Adam gradually explains his predicament. His backstory, as he understands it, is brief: His first memory is of a violent confrontation with a woman he calls only "the doctor." He fled her assault, but he's terrified she'll someday find him, so he avoids security cameras and hides most of each day. He says he's rebuilt the terminal in this room with the hopes of restoring his fragmented memories.

entries.name: Using the Terminal
entries: If the characters convince Adam they mean him no harm, he allows them to use the computer terminal while he's connected to it. The terminal screen shows the text "Project_Lamordia" followed by a prompt for a command. The terminal accepts simple text commands via a keyboard interface. Entering either of the two commands the party might have learned triggers a series of events that likely concludes the adventure; see the "{@area Concluding the Adventure|0d4|x}" section for details. Any other command entered into the terminal has no effect.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The containers around the room hold the following treasure:

items: Two {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing}
{@item Musket|XPHB} (as a rifle) with 10 {@item Firearm Bullets (10)|XPHB|Firearm Bullets}
Rare alchemical and computer components (worth 300 GP)

Assorted adventuring gear including three {@item Blanket|XPHB|Blankets}, a {@item Book|XPHB} about mushroom foraging, a plastic {@item Bucket|XPHB}, a combination {@item Lock|XPHB} (the combination is 9–4–39), five flasks of {@item Oil|XPHB}, two 30-foot coils of {@item Rope|XPHB} (as spools of plastic-coated wiring), and a {@item Shovel|XPHB}

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The characters' best means of escaping this section of Mordenheim Kinetics is by entering an appropriate command into the terminal in area S5 while Adam is attached to it.

entries.name: Helping Viktra
entries: If the characters enter "INNOVATE" into the terminal, Adam's body convulses violently before going still. He has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition for 1 hour. The doctor immediately contacts the characters via the telephone in {@area area S2|089|x}. She invites the party to take the gilded elevator in {@area area S3|090|x} to the top floor so she can thank them personally.

entries.name: Helping Adam
entries: If the characters enter "ITERATE" into the terminal, Adam's body convulses as his neuroprint resets. After a moment, he stands up. He seems quite different: calm, composed, lucid. He thanks the characters and enters an arcane series of commands into the terminal. He tells the characters that he has called the gilded elevator in {@area area S3|090|x}, which will take them to safety. If asked about his plans, Adam says he must stay here and tend to some unfinished business with the doctor.

entries.name: Gilded Elevator
entries: Whatever choice they make, the next time the characters visit the gilded elevator in the {@area area S3|090|x}, they find the elevator doors open. If the characters enter the gilded elevator, the doors slowly close before the elevator plunges dramatically into the depths of Mordenheim Kinetics. You can use this scene either as a foreboding ending to the adventure or as a segue to the "{@area Deep Freeze|0b0|x}" adventure.

entries.name: Survivor Talent
entries: If the players are playing as Lamordian survivors using the rules in the "{@area Character Options|034|x}" section, award each survivor a talent at the end of this adventure.

entries.name: Deep Freeze
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 3 Characters}

In the Cryogenics sublevel of Mordenheim Kinetics, automatons called {@creature Echo|PL|echoes} are held in cryogenic stasis for research purposes. Normally, the echoes' cryopods keep the echo units unconscious and prevent the deterioration of their humanlike tissues and delicate machinery. But the department's cryogenerator has recently reset, causing the department's cryopods to prematurely thaw.

By the time the characters arrive at the sublevel, several echoes have escaped their cryopods and turned violent as a result of a mysterious virus called Spontaneous Echo Malfunction. To escape Cryogenics alive, the party must acquire key cards from the department's feuding engineers, then reroute power from the cryogenerator to the sublevel's only elevator.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Mordenheim Kinetics' massive cryogenerator pumps frozen air into cryopods throughout the facility that contain dormant echoes. This is especially important in the Cryogenics department, where Chief Engineers {@creature Hendrik von Aubrecker|PL|Hendrik} and {@creature Gerta von Aubrecker|PL} conduct research on echo units afflicted by a mysterious virus called Spontaneous Echo Malfunction.

The cryogenerator has recently malfunctioned, and cryopods in the Cryogenics department's west wing are being insufficiently cooled. Siblings Hendrik and Gerta are currently feuding, and they refuse to cooperate long enough to reset the cryogenerator, despite frozen water flooding the facility and violent echoes awakening from stasis.

entries.name: Getting Started
entries: Use one of the adventure hooks in the "Adventure Hooks" section to explain how the characters ended up in this part of Mordenheim Kinetics, then refer to the "Beginning the Adventure" section when you're ready to begin play.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The party begins this adventure at the bottom of a dark elevator shaft. Here are some ways the characters might have gotten there:

items.name: Sanctuary Elevator
items.entry: If the characters entered the gilded elevator in the Sanctuary (see the "{@area Sanctuary|078|x}" adventure elsewhere in this section), the elevator has magically teleported them to the Cryogenics department.

items.name: Fell Down a Hole
items.entry: The characters leaned against a wall that suddenly collapsed, accidentally triggered a secret doorway, or fell into a sinkhole. At the end of a long tumble, the characters found themselves at the bottom of this cold elevator shaft.

items.name: Frozen in the Mists
items.entry: The party attempted to escape Mordenheim Kinetics through the Mists that surround the domain. After succumbing to the frigid cold of the Mists, the characters regained consciousness, shivering but unharmed, in the Cryogenics elevator shaft.

entries.name: Beginning the Adventure
entries: When you're ready to start this adventure, read the boxed text for {@area area D1|0bb|x} in the "{@area Cryogenics Locations|0ba|x}" section.

entries.name: Cryogenics Features
entries: Unless otherwise specified, the Cryogenics department has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The ceiling is 10 feet high except in {@area area D5|0d1|x}, where it is 40 feet high from the ground floor.

entries.name: Cryopods
entries: Sarcophagus-like cryopods are scattered throughout this sublevel. Each cryopod is a Large object with AC 19; HP 10; and Immunity to Cold, Poison, and Psychic damage.
