Unless noted otherwise, each cryopod in the department contains a {@creature Shattered Echo|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section) with the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. An echo regains consciousness as soon as its cryopod opens.
A cryopod requires power to function. If a cryopod has insufficient power, it opens automatically after 30 seconds.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The metal doors in this department are all unlocked except for the double doors from area D2 to area D5 (see {@area area D5 for details|0d1|x}). An unlocked door can be opened by pressing a clearly labeled button on the wall next to the door.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Pale emergency lights fill each area with {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Cryogenics Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 1.2.

entries.name: D1: Cryopod Storage
entries: This room is used to store echo units afflicted with the Spontaneous Echo Malfunction virus. When the characters first arrive here, the cryopods are drawing insufficient power.

entries.name: Cryopods
entries: Presently, this room has enough power to keep only three of the six cryopods frozen. The other three pods have already thawed; two of these are open and empty, and the third has had its lid smashed open, revealing a destroyed echo inside.

The three powered cryopods are cloudy with frost. Each contains a dormant {@creature Shattered Echo|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section) that awakens and initiates combat if the pod is opened or thaws. (See "{@area Cryogenics Features|0b5|x}" for details on cryopods.)

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Leaning against the northeast corner is a {@item Crowbar|XPHB}.

entries.name: D2: Hallway

entries.title: A lost adventurer wades through the flooded halls of the Cryogenics department.

entries: The standing water throughout this hallway is 2 feet deep, making it {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for most Small and Medium Humanoids. The door to area D1 is labeled "Cryopod Storage."

Two feet of standing water cover the floor of this frigid hallway. Steel doors with nearby electronic panels punctuate the gray walls. A computer is mounted to the wall between two of the closed doorways.
From around the corner to the north, you hear something sloshing through the water. From around the other corner, you hear something scratching and lightly banging against metal.

One of Hendrik's {@creature Created|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10c|x}" section) shambles through the hallway, fighting any creature it sees. When the characters first enter this area from area D2, the created is in the northeast corner of the corridor. It stalks the circular hallway in a counterclockwise direction.

entries.name: Floating Cryopod
entries: In the south section of the hallway, a malfunctioning cryopod floats slowly across the water. The cryopod is thawed, but its latch is stuck. The {@creature Shattered Echo|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section) trapped inside the cryopod struggles helplessly against the container.

entries.name: Cryogenerator Doors
entries: The doors to {@area area D5|0d1|x} are electromagnetically sealed. A terminal between the doors has slots for two key cards, which must be inserted simultaneously for the doors to open.

The terminal's monitor shows a blinking message: "Cryogenerator Malfunction: Operating at Reduced Power." Graphics of partially filled bars show the current distribution of power to various parts of the department. A message at the bottom of the monitor reads "To redistribute power, unlock power at locked module units, then reset Cryogenerator Mainframe." When the characters examine this monitor, show the players Handout 2: Power Distribution.

Assuming the characters haven't yet visited the operating theater or cryopod research room, a lock symbol marks the power bars next to the names of each of those rooms. The symbol changes to an unlocked state if a power spike is inserted into a workstation in that area. See {@area areas D3|0c2|x} and {@area D4|0c9|x} for more details.

entries.name: D3: Operating Theater
entries: The doors to this area are labeled "Operating Theater."

Tiered benches look down upon an operating table on the west side of the room. On the slab is a grisly sight: a mutilated mechanical body halfway through reconstruction. Attending the table is a monstrous man, more metal than flesh, his limbs all iron elbows and knifelike digits.

This augmented physician is Chief Engineer {@creature Hendrik von Aubrecker|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|115|x}" section; additional details about Hendrik's background are in the "{@area Personnel Directory|066|x}" section). He is initially {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} toward the characters, pausing his work to greet them and glean what they're doing here.
The creature on the table is one of Hendrik's created, similar to the one that roams area D2. The creature has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition when the characters first arrive.

entries.name: Speaking with Hendrik
entries: Hendrik has one key card to the cryogenerator room ({@area area D5|0d1|x}). But since he's not on speaking terms with his sister, Gerta, who has the other key card, he hasn't bothered to reset the currently malfunctioning cryogenerator.

entries.name: Hendrik's Request
entries: If the characters mention the sublevel's elevator or the malfunctioning cryogenerator, Hendrik says he's willing to help the party leave—for a favor. Read or paraphrase the following to convey Hendrik's request:

Hendrik produces a stiletto-sized metal shard and hands it to you. "Take this power spike down the hall to where my sister is working, and throttle her workstation. Just slide it into her computer or anywhere along its power cord. But make sure Gerta doesn't notice you." He also hands you a key card. "Afterward, when you restart the cryogenerator, you'll be able to divert power from her room to the elevator."

entries.name: Spiking Hendrik's Workstation
entries: A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to insert a power spike into Hendrik's computer or operating table to sabotage the engineer's work. To do so without Hendrik noticing, the character must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. Whether or not Hendrik notices, as soon as the spike is inserted, the monster on the operating table activates, as described below.
Once Hendrik's workstation is spiked, the characters can use the cryogenerator mainframe in area D5 to divert power from this room.

entries.name: Provoking Hendrik
entries: If Hendrik notices a character tampering with either his computer or the operating table, he warns the character to stop. If the character persists, Hendrik activates the machine at the foot of the operating table, which causes the monster on the table to jolt to life. This monster is a {@creature Created|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10c|x}" section) with 60 Hit Points remaining. Upon activation, the created goes berserk, as detailed in its Berserk trait, attacking the nearest creature in sight.

entries.name: D4: Cryopod Research
entries: The doors to this area are labeled "Cryopod Research."

Steel cryopods line the walls of this frigid room. Atop the chest-high steel desk in the center of the room is a humming computer terminal. A shockingly tall woman in an oversized duster stands at the desk, inputting data. As you enter the room, a resonant voice comes from the woman, though her lips don't move, and her eyes never veer from the computer monitor. "Don't let the cold out," the voice says.

The temperature in this room is below 0 degrees Fahrenheit. The woman here is {@creature Gerta von Aubrecker|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|114|x}" section; additional details about Gerta's background are in the "{@area Personnel Directory|05f|x}" section).

entries.name: Cryopods
entries: Each of the dozen cryopods here contains a dormant {@creature Shattered Echo|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section), which awakens and fights if its pod is opened. (See "{@area Cryogenics Features|0b5|x}" for details on cryopods.)

entries.name: Speaking with Gerta
entries: Gerta is initially {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} to the characters. She icily introduces herself and demands to know the party's business here.

entries.name: Gerta's Request
entries: If the characters mention Hendrik or the department's power situation, they gain Gerta's undivided attention. In exchange for giving them a key card they need to escape the sublevel, she asks the party a favor. Read or paraphrase the following to convey Gerta's request:

The titanic woman looks toward you with an unreadable expression. "I can use you," she intones. From her long jacket she draws a long metal splinter. "Use this to spike my brother's operating terminal. Beware: It will probably cause his current subject to activate." The woman removes a key card from one pocket and hands it to you. "After placing the spike, reset the mainframe to redirect power from Hendrik's terminal to the elevator."

entries.name: Spiking Gerta's Workstation
entries: A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to insert a power spike into Gerta's computer to sabotage the engineer's work. To do so without Gerta noticing, the character must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check.
Once Gerta's workstation is spiked, the characters can use the cryogenerator mainframe in area D5 to divert power from this room.

entries.name: Provoking Gerta
entries: If Gerta notices a character tampering with her computer, she booms a single warning before launching a ferocious assault against the characters.

entries.name: D5: Cryogenerator Room
entries: Both pairs of doors to this area are labeled "Cryogenerator" and are electromagnetically sealed. A placard between the doors displays a simple message above two card-sized slots: "Two key cards required for entry." The only way to open the doors is to insert two suitable key cards—such as the ones belonging to Hendrik and Gerta von Aubrecker in {@area areas D3|0c2|x} and {@area D4|0c9|x}—into the slots. Doing so causes the doors to automatically open; they remain open until the key cards are removed.
Once the characters are inside the room, read or paraphrase the following:

A massive machine of copper tubes, thick wires, and huge copper drums dominates this freezing cold chamber. Wide concrete steps lead up to the machine and its wide control terminal. Large icicles hang from every surface.

The temperature in this room is below 0 degrees Fahrenheit. The massive machine is the facility's cryogenerator. In addition to generating frozen air for cryopods throughout Mordenheim Kinetics, the cryogenerator also directs electricity throughout the Cryogenics sublevel.

entries.name: Operating the Mainframe
entries: A monitor on the mainframe's terminal mirrors the power-distribution information on the monitor in the hallway just outside this chamber (see {@area area D2|0be|x}). The mainframe's controls are intuitive enough that a character can easily deduce how to divert power from one part of the sublevel (such as the cryopods) to another (such as the elevator).

The monitor clearly shows the current power levels and the expected power levels after committing the user's change. Once the party has designated their desired power redistribution, they must reset the mainframe for the change to take effect. The mainframe monitor displays instructions for how to do this. Show the players Handout 3: Reset Instructions.
Once the Manual Safety Lever is turned, prompt your players to roll for Initiative. From this moment on, every second will count. The following happens in quick succession:

items.name: Frozen Lever
items.entry: A character who turns the mainframe's Manual Safety Lever must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take 10 ({@dice 3d6}) Cold damage from gripping the subfreezing lever.

items.name: Shaking Room
items.entry: As soon as the lever is turned, the entire room shakes violently while the cryogenerator shudders to a halt. Each creature in the room must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Falling Icicles
items.entry: Immediately after creatures make their saving throws against the shaking room, each creature in the room is struck by {@dice 1d3} falling icicles. Each icicle has a +4 attack bonus and makes a melee attack roll against the creature struck, dealing 5 ({@dice 1d10}) Piercing damage on a hit.

entries: How the characters redistribute power with the mainframe determines what threats they might face on their way toward the elevator in {@area area D1|0bb|x}. See "Concluding the Adventure" for details.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Once the characters redirect power to the elevator in {@area area D1|0bb|x}, they can use the elevator to exit the Cryogenics department.

The elevator requires 100 power units to function. Each cryopod in the Cryopod Storage room needs 50 power units to remain frozen. (The cryopods in Gerta's research lab are optimized to require much less power, though they still automatically open if power is diverted from that room.) This means that if the characters directed any power away from Cryopod Storage, one or more {@creature Shattered Echo|PL|shattered echoes} escapes from its unpowered cryopod in that area. Escaped shattered echoes race into the hallway and run amok, fighting the characters as soon as they're in sight.
Likewise, if the characters spiked either of the von Aubreckers' workstations, one or both engineers race to intercept the characters.

The characters can fight their way through their opponents or make straight for the elevator. Either way, the scene is a frantic, desperate scrabble. At your discretion, the elevator doors might not automatically close immediately after the characters enter the elevator box. Do whatever you think will ratchet up the tension and make for the best finale.

entries.name: Neural Tuning
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 5 Characters}

The Neural Tuning department is a key part of Mordenheim Kinetics' commercial arm. Here, mindless automatons wield experimental technology to scan the brains of wealthy clients. When the Mists deliver the characters to Neural Tuning's doorstep, the party must endure a gauntlet of perilous "calibration exercises" before they can face and challenge the department's megalomaniacal overseer, {@creature Rudolph von Aubrecker|PL}.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Due to increased rates of Spontaneous Echo Malfunction (see "{@creature Echo|PL|Echoes}" in the "{@area Creature Database|10d|x}" section), the Neural Tuning department has implemented stringent calibration tests for potential neuroprint donors. Such tests are meant to ensure a higher rate of quality neuroprints, but Biotechnical Director Rudolph von Aubrecker enforces the protocol haphazardly. The director's chief concern is the amassing of neuroprints, no matter their condition. Countless donors have suffered—or outright perished—from Neural Tuning's preliminary exercises. To Rudolph, the lives lost are simply the cost of scientific advancement.

entries.name: Getting Started
entries: Use one of the adventure hooks in the "Adventure Hooks" section to explain how the characters ended up in this part of Mordenheim Kinetics, then refer to the "Beginning the Adventure" section when you're ready to begin play.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The characters begin this adventure in a brilliantly lit hallway of mirrorlike walls. Here are some ways the characters might have gotten there:

items.name: Lost in the Maze
items.entry: While exploring Mordenheim Kinetics, the characters came upon an innocuous door with bright light streaming through the cracks. Opening the door unleashed a brilliant light, and when the characters regained their senses, they found themselves in this hallway, the original doorway nowhere in sight.

items.name: Not Heaven
items.entry: After being slain elsewhere in Mordenheim Kinetics, the characters came to, somehow alive, in this hallway of piercing white light, walking toward a door.

items.name: Into the Mirror
items.entry: The characters' last memory is of finding an ominous looking glass or reflecting pool they felt strangely compelled to look into. When they looked away from the mirror, the characters found themselves in this hallway of silvery walls.

entries.name: Beginning the Adventure
entries: When you're ready to start this adventure, read the boxed text for {@area area N1|0df|x} in the "{@area Neural Tuning Locations|0de|x}" section.

entries.name: Neural Tuning Features
entries: Unless otherwise specified, the Neural Tuning department has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The ceiling is 20 feet high except in {@area area N1|0df|x}, where it is only 10 feet high, and {@area area N7|0fd|x}, where it is 50 feet high.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The metal doors in this department are locked with a complex lock of good quality (1 minute to pick, {@dc 15}), except for the doors to {@area area N4|0f1|x}, which are unlocked. Rudolph von Aubrecker can remotely unlock any of the doors from anywhere else in the department.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Fluorescent lights fill each area with Bright Light.

entries.name: Neural Tuning Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 1.3.

entries.name: N1: Bright Hallway

entries: Bright light fills this narrow hallway, whose walls are silvery and reflective. The only egress is a metal double door to the east. The door automatically closes and reopens, stuck on a fallen ladder lying on the floor in the door sensor's path. A speaker near the doorway repeats a recorded message: "Obstruction detected. Please unblock door."

The door here normally opens automatically if it detects a creature within 5 feet of its west side, then closes once the creature is clear of the doorway. From the east, the door remains closed and locked.
Presently, a maintenance Ladder has fallen in the way of the door, preventing it from closing and locking. If the Ladder is removed, the door is able to close and lock as normal.

entries.name: N2: Calibration Chamber

entries.title: Parts of Mordenheim Kinetics' Neural Tuning department have fallen into ruin.

entries: A staircase wraps around the west side of this large auditorium, connecting to a balcony that overlooks the floor below. A large projector screen on the east wall is flanked by two loudspeakers. Chairs arranged in a triangle face the screen. Exits include doors to the west and south.
Four people, apparently strangers, mill about the room, examining their surroundings and making occasional chitchat.
The four people here are {@creature Echo|PL|Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10d|x}" section). Following are the echoes' names and brief summaries of their backgrounds:

items.name: Alexis Melodious
items.entry: Alexis is a famous pop star and hedonistic diva.

items.name: Bryant Epsilon
items.entry: Bryant is a quiet tech worker who has fuzzy memories of being a midlevel engineer at Mordenheim Kinetics.

items.name: Jessita Cruz
items.entry: Jessita is a semifamous philanthropist with a track record of donating to far-fetched causes.

items.name: Wilbert Monroe
items.entry: Wilbert is a wealthy entrepreneur who's invested a fortune in Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Speaking with the Echoes
entries: Each echo contains the neuroprint of one of Mordenheim Kinetics' wealthy clients. They've all recently awoken in artificial bodies. Like the characters, they've found themselves in the Neural Tuning department by chance. Beyond this, each echo knows virtually nothing about their situation. Though obviously not human, none of the echoes know precisely what they are.

entries.name: Tuning Procedure
entries: Once all the characters are in the room and they've had a moment to orient themselves, read or paraphrase the following:

The projector flickers on and beams an image of a pale face with hard features onto the screen. "Hello, prospective donors," the face says with scripted enthusiasm. "Allow me to formally welcome you to the Mordenheim Kinetics Neuroprint Screening Program. I am Director Rudolph von Aubrecker.

"If you're here, congratulations! You are a candidate to receive a neuroscan. Before we officially meet, you'll undergo a few basic calibration exercises. In this room, you'll be exposed to a fifteen-second tone, which may be painful. Please wait patiently for the tone to end, then proceed to the next room."

The projection ends, and a different robotic voice comes on over an unseen wall speaker: "Warning: The tone may have undesirable effects on Mordenheim Kinetics echo units. Echoes in the area, please leave via the nearest exit immediately."

Following the message, a loud tone blares from the room's two wall speakers. The four echoes in this room panic immediately. At this point, ask your players to roll Initiative, and roll Initiative for the echoes.

The tone blares for 2 rounds. While the tone blares, the echoes race toward the nearest doors and try to exit the room. Unless the characters have already unlocked them, the doors to the south are locked (see the "{@area Neural Tuning Features|0da|x}" section). If the Ladder was removed from the doorway to {@area area N1|0df|x}, that door is also closed and locked.

entries.name: Tone Effects
entries: While the tone blares, each creature that starts its turn in this room must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or take 5 ({@dice 2d4}) Thunder damage. Echoes automatically fail the save. An echo that fails the save twice in a row has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn, when it becomes a {@creature Shattered Echo|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section). Shattered echoes fight the nearest non-echo creature in sight.

entries.name: Loudspeakers
entries: Each speaker on the wall is a Small object with AC 13; Hit Points 10; and Immunity to Poison, Psychic, and Thunder damage. The tone ends if both speakers are destroyed.

entries.name: End of Calibration
entries: If there are any shattered echoes in the room, Director Rudolph waits until they are destroyed before opening the doors to area N3. Otherwise, he remotely opens the doors to area N3 as soon as the tone ends. Any surviving echoes that didn't become shattered echoes are too scared to leave this room.

entries.name: N3: Proprioception Test

entries: A large projector screen hangs on the west wall of this broad laboratory chamber. Projected on the screen is the message "Quintessential Qualities of Musical Virtuosi" and a list of different types of instruments. Facing the screen are four chairs with a microphone dangling between them.

The room's north wall is covered in lockers stocked with every instrument imaginable. South, two automatons operate a complex audio console. To the east, two sets of double-doors are potential exits, in addition to the doors to the northwest.

Different instruments of every type are stored in the lockers along the north wall. The two automatons are {@creature Empty Echo|PL|Empty Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10e|x}" section) that type mindlessly at their terminals.

entries.name: List of Instrument Families
entries: The screen on the west wall displays a list of instrument families and "ideal qualities" for performers of each instrument family. When the characters examine this monitor, show the players Handout 4: Quintessential Qualities of Musical Virtuosi.

entries.title: Handout 4: Quintessential Qualities of Musical Virtuosi

entries.name: Proprioception Test
entries: After the characters have had a moment to examine their surroundings, read or paraphrase the following to begin this room's puzzle:

The director's voice crackles from an unseen speaker: "Now I will test your proprioception and self-awareness. Please select and play an instrument that best expresses your abilities. Once you play an appropriate instrument, you'll hear a chime." After a pause, the director adds, "And please don't muck about. The automatons in that room are quite sensitive to sonic disturbances."

Rudolph expects each character to choose an instrument that corresponds to that character's highest ability score. The instrument families listed on the monitor correspond to the six ability scores: percussion (Strength), string (Dexterity), brass (Constitution), electronic (Intelligence), woodwind (Wisdom), and vocals (Charisma).

To solve the puzzle, each character must play a musical instrument that corresponds to the character's highest ability score. For example, if a character's highest ability score is Dexterity, the character should play a string instrument. A character with multiple highest ability scores should play an instrument from any of the corresponding instrument families.

entries.name: Solving the Puzzle
entries: For each character that plays a suitable instrument, a chime rings out over the room's speaker. Once all the characters have played an instrument corresponding to the character's highest ability score, Director Rudolph thanks the group for their cooperation, remotely unlocks the double door to the northeast, and asks them to proceed.

entries.name: Failing the Puzzle
entries: If any character plays three incorrect instruments in a row, the two automatons in this room convulse violently and become two {@creature Shattered Echo|PL|Shattered Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section) that fight the party. In this case, Rudolph unlocks the doors to {@area area N5|0f3|x} only after the shattered echoes are destroyed.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: One of the instruments in this room is an {@item Instrument of Illusions|XDMG}.

entries.name: N4: Service Elevator
entries: The doors to this service elevator are unlocked.

This wide service elevator is empty except for a screen on the wall that reads "Elevator disabled. Insert emergency lever to operate." In the floor near the screen is a four-inch-square rectangular socket.

The elevator can't be operated until its missing lever is installed. A character who takes the {@action Search|XPHB} action to examine the socket and succeeds on a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check sees that the socket is quite complex and requires a lever with a specific form factor. (Rudolph's arm is a suitable lever; see area N5.)

entries.name: N5: Neuroscan Booths

entries: An array of ten-foot-tall booths line the walls of this long chamber. Each booth includes a chair. Above each chair, a metal helmetlike device is attached via cables to a complex computer terminal. Various personal effects are scattered about some of the booths. Wide double doors lead north, south, and east.

Four humanlike automatons and a fifth figure stand near the chamber's entryway and motion for you to take a seat. The fifth figure is a mechanical monstrosity, barely human except for the face of Director Rudolph von Aubrecker stretched across a skull-like appendage. Behind the director's face is a brain suspended in a jar of fluid.
The doors to the east are jammed by rubble.

In this room, donors have their brains scanned using the machinery in the booths. The resulting neuroscan data is stored in a glass canister, which must be taken to {@area area N7|0fd|x} for processing and storage.

Director {@creature Rudolph von Aubrecker|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|116|x}" section; additional details about Rudolph's background are in the "{@area Personnel Directory|06d|x}" section) greets the characters as soon as they arrive. While he describes the neuroscan process to the party, his attendants, four {@creature Empty Echo|PL|Empty Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10e|x}" section), measure the characters' heads and attempt to escort the characters to the available booths. The attendants are programmed to force the characters into the booths, and each uses [Tooltip Not Found] to grapple or shove a character into place. The attendants don't try to deal damage to the characters.

entries.name: Rudolph's Arm/Elevator Lever
entries: If the party has already been to {@area area N4|0f1|x}, a character who takes the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine Rudolph and succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check realizes that Rudolph's mechanical arms have the same attachment mechanism as the missing lever in the service elevator. A creature can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to remove Rudolph's arm by succeeding on a {@dc 20} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. If Rudolph is willing or dead or has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, the creature automatically succeeds on the check.

entries.name: Speaking to Director Rudolph
entries: Director Rudolph encourages the characters to take seats in any of the booths around the room. If the characters say they're here by accident or ask to leave, Rudolph shakes his head emphatically. He tells the party that it would be a terrible waste not to acquire neuroprints of such marvelous specimens, then implores them once again to sit in the neuroscan booths. "The pain will be temporary," the doctor says, "but your contributions to science shall be everlasting."

entries.name: Neuroscan Procedure
entries: A creature that starts its turn in a neuroscan booth must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 13}) from steel-reinforced straps that extend from the booth's underside and wrap around the creature. While Grappled in this way, the creature also has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition.

At the end of its turn, a creature Grappled by a neuroscan booth makes a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw against the metal helmet that automatically lowers onto the creature's head. On a failed save, the creature takes 10 ({@dice 3d6}) Psychic damage as the helmet violently extracts a digital copy of the creature's mind. A creature that fails the save also experiences a random side effect from the neuroscan. Roll on or choose a result from the Neuroscan Side Effects table to determine the side effect.

entries.caption: Neuroscan Side Effects
rows: Becomes dreadfully frightened by wriggly creatures like eels, snakes, and worms—or loses this fear if the character already had it.
Can taste iron whenever the character sees or thinks of the color blue.
Forgets the details and history of a relationship with a random fellow party member.
Gains the uncanny memory of being a fish living in a fish tank.

entries.name: Fighting Back
entries: If the characters fight Rudolph or any of this room's attendants, Rudolph panics and flees to {@area area N7|0fd|x}. As he passes through area N6, Rudolph corrupts the echoes in that area (see "Corrupting the Echoes" in {@area area N6|0fb|x}).

entries.name: Agreeing to the Procedure
entries: If the characters all submit to the neuroscan procedure without any opposition, Rudolph thanks them for their cooperation. In this case, he willingly gives them one of his arms and gives them instructions on how to leave the Neural Tuning department via the service elevator ({@area area N4|0f1|x}). See the "{@area Concluding the Adventure|0d4|x}" section for more details.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the characters search the neuroscan booths, they find the following treasures:

items: {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Aura of Purity|XPHB}
A fine gold chain set with a fire opal (worth 2,500 GP)

entries.name: N6: Hallway
entries: Three {@creature Echo|PL|Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|10d|x}" section) sit docilely in chairs along the perimeter of this hallway.

entries.name: Corrupting the Echoes
entries: While at the terminal at the east end of this hall, Rudolph can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to enter a special command. The command causes each echo connected to a machine in this hallway to have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn, after which the echo becomes a {@creature Shattered Echo|PL} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section). The shattered echoes join Rudolph at area N7 and obediently follow his orders.

entries.name: N7: Neuroprint Database

entries: Humming terminals line the walls of this brightly lit server room. In the room's center is a tower of spinning fans, computer interfaces, and glowing green tubes. The tower is connected with thick, bundled cords to power generators on the room's north, east, and south walls.

Cylinders of freshly extracted neuroprints are taken to this room for processing and storage. The tower in the room's center acts like a centrifuge, spinning cylinders of raw neuroprint data to separate digitized memories from their plasmatic substrate.

If the characters' earlier interaction with Rudolph in {@area area N5|0f3|x} turned violent, {@creature Rudolph von Aubrecker|PL} and three {@creature Shattered Echo|PL|Shattered Echoes} (see the "{@area Creature Database|110|x}" section) make a final stand against the characters here. In this case, read or paraphrase the following:

Director Rudolph and three hunched-over automatons guard the tower. "That's quite enough," the director calls over the roaring machinery. "Don't come any closer! You meddle in matters of genius you could scarcely understand."

entries.name: Damaging the Database
entries: Each of the three power lines connected to the central database is a Large object with AC 14, Hit Points 40, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage.

Destroying a power line releases a shock wave in a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the power line. Each creature in that area makes a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 ({@dice 4d6}) Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
If the characters damage the power lines, Rudolph screams for the party to stop. If two of the power lines are destroyed, Rudolph surrenders and tells the characters he'll do whatever they ask.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Once the characters have the emergency lever for the service elevator in {@area area N4|0f1|x}, they can use the elevator to escape the Neural Tuning department.

Where the service elevator takes the characters is up to you. It might take them to another Domain of Dread, to their places of origin, or to another part of Mordenheim Kinetics. If you want to keep the party in Mordenheim Kinetics, see the "{@area Other Adventures|104|x}" section for ideas for additional adventures.

entries.name: Stuck in Neural Tuning
entries: If the characters can't defeat Rudolph, he subjects them to further testing and calibration exercises. At best, the characters' functions are reduced to those of obedient automatons. At worst, the experiments ultimately leave the characters brain-dead. In either case, the characters are doomed to serve the evil director for as long as he can maintain their bodies—which, thanks to the director's scientific talent, could be a very long time.

entries.name: Neuroprint Clones
entries: For characters who underwent the neuroscan process, there's no telling where their digital copies might ultimately end up. In this case, even if the characters die or otherwise fail to escape Neural Tuning, you can let your players continue to use their characters in subsequent adventures with the understanding that they're not the characters' original incarnations. To further drive this point home, you could ask your players to revise their characters to have the Reborn species instead of their original species. Taking this route, the party can continue their adventures together, but they'll always know that their original forms could still be out there somewhere.

entries.name: Other Adventures
entries: If you want to continue the party's adventures in Mordenheim Kinetics, here are some ideas for additional adventures in this Domain of Dread:

items.name: Bride of Adam
items.entry: After resigning himself to his fate as an immortal monster, {@creature Adam|PL} enlists the characters to help him construct a companion of artificial flesh just like him.

items.name: Data Hunters
items.entry: Several {@creature K-Nine|PL|K-Nines} have somehow been injected with neuroprints and now possess super intelligence. The mechanical hounds are systematically hunting down and killing their neuroprints' original donors. A donor on the run finds the party and begs for help.

items.name: Into the Dreamscape
items.entry: {@creature CEO Viktra Mordenheim|PL|Viktra Mordenheim} invents a machine that allows her to physically experience events recorded in any neuroprint. Obsessed with understanding the error of her failed experiment Adam, the doctor locks herself in the original neuroprint she used to create the monster. To escape Mordenheim Kinetics, the characters must connect to the same neuroprint, find Viktra in the dreamscape, and convince the doctor to return to the realm of reality.

items.name: Robot Army
items.entry: Deep in the bowels of Mordenheim Kinetics' hellish forge-factories, a disgruntled technologist assembles an army of weaponized echo units to overthrow the company's CEO.

items.name: Secret of Life
items.entry: A gravely wounded cleric from the world of Greyhawk is drawn into the domain of Mordenheim Kinetics. Viktra Mordenheim seeks the cleric's knowledge of resurrection magic for her own aims. The characters find the cleric first. Before the cleric can help the party escape the domain, the characters must guard the cleric from Viktra's servants and find a cure for the cleric's mysterious ailment.

items.name: Supercomputer's Playthings
items.entry: A self-aware computer virus lures the characters to the research and development building it's taken over. The virus controls every aspect of the building, including hologram projectors, stray echo units, and security systems. To escape the virus's wicked games, the party must devise a way to outwit their superintelligent captor.

data.name: Creature Database

entries.title: A Reborn That Has Become a Hive Host.

entries: This section includes rules for turning existing creatures into kinetic creations and details on the specific monsters that roam Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Kinetic Creations
entries: Kinetic creations are fabricated life-forms that roam Mordenheim Kinetics. A kinetic creation can resemble a naturally occurring creature, but it is either an artificial horror or a creature so transformed that it can no longer rightly be thought of in its original context.
You can use the following rules to convert monsters from other settings into kinetic creations that fit into the setting of Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Base Kinetic Traits
entries: You can make any creature a kinetic creation by giving it the following traits:

items.name: Cursed Creation
items.entry: The creature can't leave Mordenheim Kinetics, and its creature type changes to Construct.

items.name: Mechanical Physiology
items.entry: The creature has Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Additional Kinetic Traits
entries: At your discretion, a kinetic creation can also have one or more of the following traits:

items.name: Guided Ballistics
items.entry: The creature's ranged attacks ignore {@table Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} and {@table Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}.

items.name: Hive Host
items.entry: Swarms of Tiny Beasts are initially {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to the creature.

items.name: Nanogel Body
items.entry: The creature can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

items.name: Optical Camouflage
items.entry: The creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks. Additionally, if the creature spends at least 1 minute without moving or taking actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions, it has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. The condition ends if the creature moves or takes an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.

items.name: Organic Assimilation (2/Day)
items.entry: If the creature starts its turn in the same space as a dead creature that is Large or smaller, the corpse is destroyed, leaving behind only what it was wearing or carrying.

items.name: Overclocked
items.entry: The creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength saving throws and {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.

items.name: Predictive Algorithms
items.entry: The creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@action opportunity attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} and Dexterity saving throws.

items.name: Self-Repairing Nanodrones (1/Day)
items.entry: At the start of its turn, the creature can end one of the following conditions on itself: {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB}.

items.name: Thermal Imaging
items.entry: The creature can see any creature or object that has a temperature of at least 80 degrees Fahrenheit as long as the target is within 60 feet and not behind {@table Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}.

entries.name: Bestiary
entries: This section presents stat blocks in alphabetical order for monsters that appear in Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Adam
entries: {@i Dr. Mordenheim's Greatest Regret}

Dr. Viktra Mordenheim's greatest invention is also her worst mistake: Adam, an automaton imprinted with the neuroprint of Viktra's dead lover. Adam's hulking figure and disheveled appearance are a result of his final struggle with Viktra, which also resulted in Adam's memories being corrupted. He now haunts the halls of Mordenheim Kinetics, searching for clues that might explain his monstrous nature and why the doctor hunts him.
Adam is described in more detail in the "{@area Personnel Directory|058|x}" section.

entries.name: CEO Viktra Mordenheim
entries: {@i President and Founder of Mordenheim Kinetics}
The founder and president of Mordenheim Kinetics is an eccentric visionary, unparalleled technologist, and notorious recluse.

The stat block in this section is based on the Viktra Mordenheim stat block in {@book Ravenloft: The Horrors Within|RHW|2|Viktra Mordenheim}. You can use the additional details and rules in that book to further describe Viktra and emphasize her ability to control her domain.
Viktra is described in more detail in the "{@area Personnel Directory|04f|x}" section.

entries.name: Created
entries: {@i Monstrous Artifice of Life}

The created are Chief Engineer {@area Hendrik von Aubrecker|115|x} attempt to replicate and improve upon Dr. Mordenheim's incredible humanlike automaton, {@area Adam|10a|x} (detailed elsewhere in this section).

At his project's outset, Hendrik crafted a custom neuroprint by combining his own neuroprint with neuroprints from each of his siblings. Hendrik injects all of his created with the same copy of this chimeric neuroprint, but no two created are the same. Each created manifests a unique combination of the three von Aubreckers' intellects, obsessions, and personality flaws. The only things the created have in common are their violent dispositions toward anyone but the von Aubreckers and their tendency to go haywire when physically damaged.

Though his ultimate goal is to perfectly replicate the human form, Hendrik is no artist, and he lacks access to realistic fabricated flesh and textiles. He clumsily enrobes his creations with what materials he has on hand—contrivances that only emphasize the created's artificial nature. Roll on or choose a result from the Created Facade table to inspire the eerie appearance of a created.

entries.caption: Created Facade
rows: Clothes patched together from discarded lab coats, protective goggles, and disposable gloves.
Hair made from tangles of copper wiring and plastic tubing.
Nonfunctional extra limbs stolen from other created.
Digits and extremities cobbled together from ordinary office stationery.
A mirror for a face.
Jewelry made from microscope lenses, circuit wires, and electrical diodes.

entries.name: Echoes
entries: {@i Mechanical Memory Vessels}

Echoes are advanced bipedal constructs designed in the manufacturing wing of Mordenheim Kinetics. Each echo is built to house the digitized memories and personality of a specific "agent"—a neuroprint, typically donated by one of Mordenheim Kinetics' unconscionably wealthy clients.

Before its neuroprint is injected, an echo's chassis is called an empty echo. Both echoes and empty echoes are susceptible to a mysterious syndrome called Spontaneous Echo Malfunction, which corrupts the echo's neuroprint receptor and transforms the echo into a shattered echo.

entries.name: Empty Echo
entries: An echo is "empty" until imprinted with its agent's neuroprint. While empty, an echo possesses just enough computing power to move around and perform basic tasks on its own, though it lacks the ability to reason, feel emotions, or form memories.

Unsupervised, empty echoes have the unsettling tendency to self-activate, leave their storage units, and wander the halls of Mordenheim Kinetics. Even more unsettlingly, an empty echo's only means of verbal communication is to emit an ear-piercing screech. Technicians are advised to wear hearing protection at all times when working on empty echoes.

entries.name: Echo
entries: Once an empty echo is injected with a neuroprint, it becomes a fully functional echo. Beneath its sturdy mechanical frame, an echo has all the same memories and personality traits as its neuroprint donor, also called the echo's agent.

As an echo, an agent retains all of its learned skills and talents but none of its muscle memory. It can take months or even years before an agent is able to perform once-routine activities in its new echo body. Most echoes succumb to Spontaneous Echo Malfunction before regaining their full motoric functions.

entries.name: Shattered Echo
entries: A shattered echo is an echo that has undergone Spontaneous Echo Malfunction (SEM). Both empty echoes and neuroprint-injected echoes are susceptible to the phenomenon, which has no known cause. Signs of a shattered echo include unpredictable movements, murderous outbursts, and violent hallucinations. Once an echo has shattered, it's impossible to repair the echo's neuroprint or return the echo to working condition.

If a shattered echo had an agent before undergoing SEM, it often retains corrupted fragments of its agent's memories and personality. Such shattered echoes might attempt to reenact disjointed memories or chirp half-remembered bits of overheard dialogue. Though such behaviors may give the impression of a latent intellect, they're in fact nothing more than misfiring bits of computer code.

entries.name: K-Nine
entries: {@i Canine-Shaped Combat Droid}
Shaped like a hunting dog and programmed to be five times as vicious, the Mordenheim Kinetics K-Nine unit is a combat machine designed for tactical warfare and conflict suppression.

When funding for Mordenheim Kinetics' primary ventures started to dwindle, Dr. Mordenheim turned to less scrupulous clients for capital. The K-Nine is one of the company's most successful creations developed for military defense contractors and private mercenary groups.

Before Mordenheim Kinetics' fall into ruin, K-Nine prototypes and deactivated units decorated the facility's lobbies. Now, packs of the mechanical hounds stalk the campus like feral wolves, hunting down and forcibly disabling escaped experiments and wayward visitors alike.
When it comes to home intruder prevention, give Fido a break. Protect your property with a pack of K-Nine Domicile Defense Units. Now with Piston-Powered Paw & Jaw Technology.
Mordenheim Kinetics K-Nine: Man's Worst Enemy™
entries.from: Copy from Mordenheim Kinetics' Canceled Consumer K-Nine Program

entries.name: Von Aubreckers
entries: {@i Unscrupulous Sibling Scientists}

The von Aubreckers are sibling scientists who work throughout Mordenheim Kinetics as senior engineers. Though they report to {@area Viktra Mordenheim|10b|x} (detailed elsewhere in this section), the detached doctor gives her senior staff a dangerous degree of autonomy. Each sibling exploits this freedom to pursue passion projects—including dramatic body modifications and cybernetic augmentations.
For more details about the von Aubreckers, see the "{@book Personnel Directory|PL|3}" section.

entries.name: Gerta von Aubrecker
entries: Towering, fierce Gerta may be the youngest von Aubrecker, but she looms over her brothers in both stature and force of personality. Gerta's custom plasteel skeleton and weatherproofed chassis protect her from the dangers of her work with dormant {@area empty echoes|10e|x} (detailed elsewhere in this section) in the Cryogenics department.

entries.name: Hendrik von Aubrecker
entries: Hendrik has modified his body to truly monstrous effect. In place of bones and organs, Hendrik has a carbon fiber exoskeleton and a self-recharging engine in his rib cage. Hydraulic pistons give Hendrik incredible speed and enable him to deliver devastating blows. For particularly elusive enemies, Hendrik employs syringes full of potent sedatives from his third arm.

entries.name: Rudolph von Aubrecker
entries: Despite his near-total transformation into a technological monster, Rudolph remains the most charming of the von Aubrecker siblings. All that remain of the elder brother's original form are his handsome face and formidable brain; the latter is augmented by cybernetic enhancements that amplify his mental powers to supernatural levels.

Begin record. Postmortem log, round nine-seven-gamma, trial six-eight-three. Summary: Hallucinatory glitches continue. Elaboration: Installation of premature awakening inhibitor has proven insufficient to counteract Spontaneous Echo Malfunction. Results of trial six-eight-three confirm that neuroprint incompatibility remains a serious issue and that SEM has now eclipsed Premature Awakening Syndrome in prevalence as well as severity. Rate of SEM incidence is sixty-seven percent higher among test units thawed from cryogenic stasis. Latest recorded echo-neuroprint rejection rate... thirty-six percent, up from the previous round's twenty-one percent. Despite the risks of continued failure, I feel we must continue testing the latest neurotransference algorithm.
